title: What Is a Smart Lock? Why I Recommend This Security Upgrade for Everyone
snippet: A smart lock upgrade offers excellent utility and control without sacrificing privacy.
fullText:
When I’m asked about smart home gadgets, I typically suggest people start at their front door, such as with a video doorbell or smart lock. Smart locks, in particular, are an obvious first step (and only step, if you prefer) into smart home tech, and they can benefit nearly anyone with a front door.

But many people without a smart lock in their lives still don’t know what it is, how it works or why they should spend money on one. It’s time for a clear explanation of this important home technology, and why I’m such a fan.

			

			

							
		

	

		

			Best Smart Locks of 2026: Excellent Door Upgrades
		

					

These powerful, connected locks are useful every day. We've tested the latest to find the best.

						

		

Smart lock basics

Retrofits typically only require replacing the thumb turn.

Amazon

A smart lock replaces the standard deadbolt found on nearly any front door (and many other doors) in a residential building. Many models replace the deadbolt entirely, which tends to allow extra features like keypads and fingerprint readers. Other types replace only the indoor thumb turn, the knob used to move the deadbolt — a smart lock style called a retrofit — which is often cheaper and easier to install. Either way, the door handle below the lock is usually left untouched.

Once set up, the smart lock connects to your Wi-Fi router and lets you control it from your phone using a corresponding app. This allows you to operate the lock remotely, anywhere you can connect to the internet (like at work, or on vacation). That ability comes with several valuable tricks.

The inside thumbturn is usually the only part of a lock replaced in a retrofit.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

With remote locking and unlocking, you don’t have to be at home to let a pet sitter or guest inside. Most smart lock apps also let you create temporary passcodes or digital passkeys for guests, which grant access and then auto-delete after the timeframe ends.

These locks can also send alerts to your phone, notifying you when the door is locked or unlocked. You can review a history of locking/unlocking in the app, or even set the door to automatically lock after a set amount of time, so no one ever forgets to lock the door again. Those features are also handy for keeping track of someone in an aging-in-place situation.

That’s only the start of what a high-quality smart lock can do.

Smart lock access methods

From keypads and digital wallet keys to fingerprints, smart locks offer new ways to protect your home.Schlage

Another one of my favorite things about smart locks is the different access methods they open up (heh), some of which may be far better for your daily life than the classic key.

Most locks not only have app controls but can sense when an authenticated mobile device is near, and automatically unlock with a swipe. That’s getting both easier and more common now that the Aliro protocol has been established this year, helping smart locks connect to digital wallets (Google, Apple, Samsung and so on) that you probably already use, making pass management very easy.

Other locks focus on fingerprint scanners, a biometric option that I found highly accurate and quite speedy in all my testing. It takes only a couple of minutes to add your family’s fingerprints, and then you don’t have to worry about people losing their keys or needing access to the home when you aren’t around.

More advanced smart locks can do a little of everything.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Some people may prefer to stick with the classic keypad, another common component of smart locks. Keypads let you change and swap codes and issue temporary codes to workers or visitors, which isn’t as easy to manage with a fingerprint sensor. Both work well in my testing, but keypads take longer to set up and the different designs may confuse some first-time users.

A number of smart locks combine all these access options and more, so you can choose your preferred method. Most include an emergency key slot or standard key slot, too. However, some of the most advanced models I’ve tested skip old-school keys entirely, so users don’t have to worry about anyone picking the lock.

Smart lock installation and compatibility

Smart lock installation is surprisingly easy if you’ve got a screwdriver and a little time.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Don’t worry about how difficult a smart lock is to install. As I mentioned, they’ll work with most standard deadbolt designs, and are typically a DIY project. You shouldn’t need more than a sturdy screwdriver for a full deadbolt replacement.

Most locks have alternative options for slightly different deadbolt placements. Take a look at my guide on how to install a smart lock to learn – well, everything you need to know.

Important note: Renters should also check their lease and see what their landlord or property management company says. Typically, installing a new deadbolt is a step too far for tenants, although a retrofit may be more permissible. But landlords usually prefer to handle anything related to locks themselves. There are even smart locks made specifically for them.

Battery life and smart locks

Batteries are always installed on the inside housing, typically AAs. 

Tyler Lacoma/CNET

How do smart locks accomplish all their tricks and maintain their Wi-Fi connections? The lock’s indoor housing also houses the battery. Some locks run on two to four AA batteries. Others use proprietary rechargeable batteries that you need to remove and recharge from time to time.

Either way, these batteries typically last at least a few months and up to a year, depending on how often the door is activated. Apps generally give you warnings or alerts when battery power is low. Some models are designed to last longer, like Lockly’s Lyro Lasta, which packs in eight batteries and adds a sleep mode to help the lock last up to three years.

Smart locks include emergency ways to charge up and unlock the deadbolt when necessary, like if your Wi-Fi is down or the batteries suddenly fail.

			

			

							
		

	

		

			Best Budget Smart Locks for 2026: Affordable and Tough
		

					

After testing smart locks from all the top brands, I've found the best picks for you and your wallet.

						

		

Smart lock costs

So, I’ve praised this home add-on pretty thoroughly, but how much will something like this cost? Smart locks aren’t especially cheap, but they offer a wide range of prices and models, so most buyers can find an option that works for them.

If you’re focused on your budget and want to save money, I suggest looking for a retrofit model for your current deadbolt. Basic retrofits only cost around $70 to $100, as you can see on my best affordable smart locks list. You can even find some full deadbolt replacements for around $100, such as from Wyze, but these are rarer.

The most compact and advanced the lock, the more expensive they tend to be.Tyler Lacoma/CNEt

In the $150 to $200 range, smart locks start gaining many more capabilities, including advanced access options, better durability ratings and more compact sizes. I suggest most homeowners start here if they’re looking for a worthwhile upgrade with plenty of useful capabilities.

At $250 and above, you start paying more for the top-performing smart locks with the most high-tech features. One of my top picks, for example, is the Yale Assure Lock 2 at $260. There’s also the “invisible” Level Lock Pro at $349 and the futuristic, glowing panel of the Schlage Sense Pro at $396.

Best smart lock brands

Head over to my smart lock buying guide for much more information on picking a lock that’s right for you, and what to consider when buying. Many companies offer smart locks, so you’ll have your pick of options. Some of my favorites that I’ve personally tested are Schlage, Yale, Level and August, all reliable brands with a history in locking technologies.

Since many locks are compatible with the smart home standard Matter, you don’t always have to use the brand’s own app to control them. Locks tend to work well with Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and SmartThings, although you find your control options more limited when it comes to complex settings.

Now you know everything important about smart locks, so when are you going to get your own? My guide to the best smart locks is one of the best spots to get started.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Tyler Lacoma

title: Motorola confirms ‘Signature 27’ debut next week alongside new Snapdragon chips
snippet: As part of next week’s Snapdragon Summit, Motorola has confirmed that it will be detailing its new “Signature 27” device on September 22. more…
fullText:
As part of next week’s Snapdragon Summit, Motorola has confirmed that it will be detailing its new “Signature 27” device on September 22.

In a teaser on social media, Motorola has confirmed that its new “Signature 27” smartphone will be detailed on September 22. It’s unclear if this is a full launch or just a teaser – the first Motorola Signature launched in January of this year, so it’s an accelerated timeline if nothing else.

The teaser video shows a green device with a fabric-like back, cameras with a Dolby Vision mark, and a focus on a pretty big lens too. Other details are unknown, but the timing is noteworthy. September 22 is also the first day of Qualcomm’s annual Snapdragon Summit, the event that launches each year’s new Snapdragon flagship chipset. The first Signature ran on Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 rather than the Elite, though, so it’s hard to know for sure what’s planned.

A similar teaser popped up on Motorola’s website earlier this month, including on its US page, implying the “Signature 27” might make its way to the States.

title: Google Home MCP lets Antigravity, Claude, OpenClaw, & more control your smart home
snippet: Google today announced “Home MCP” to let your personal AI agent interact with your smart home devices via the Model Context Protocol. more…
fullText:
Google today announced “Home MCP” to let your personal AI agent interact with your smart home devices via the Model Context Protocol.

This allows Google Antigravity, Claude, Hermes, OpenClaw, and any other agent that supports calling MCP tools to “interact with all of the devices and event history in the Google Home ecosystem.” 

This includes Google Nest cameras and doorbells, Nest Thermostats, Matter light bulbs, and beyond. Example use cases include:

Cross-Camera Analysis: Ask your agent what the kids did when they got home from school, and it will provide a summary across all of your cameras of what they did and show you the clips

Analyze home history: Your agent can use your device state history to track how many loads of laundry were done in a week, or how long the lights were left on.

Interact with you via voice: If your agent is completing an asynchronous or proactive task,  it can send you an audio message over your Google Home speaker when it’s finished.

Build a dashboard: Your agent can build you a custom dashboard that provides a view of your smart home tailored just to you.

Google frames this as giving your agent “real-world physical context—allowing it to analyze and answer questions about home activity, summarize camera footage across rooms, manage devices on your behalf, or even create your own smart home dashboards using everyday language.”

	

On the security and privacy front, Home MCP “enforces rate limits and safety protections, such as prohibiting sensitive actions like unlocking doors.” Google cautions about how:

However, depending on your agent, connecting it to Home MCP can result in unexpected or even undesired behavior. Carefully review developer policies and terms of service.

As of today, Home MCP is rolling out for Google Home Premium Advanced users in US English. The setup process involves creating a Google Cloud project and then configuring it to use Home MCP. 

…simply provide the MCP configuration details to your agent and ask it to set it up. Your agent will ask you to sign in and grant permissions. After that, you’re ready to go. For complete setup guides, visit the Google Home Developer Center.

title: AI hallucination nearly triggers US military operation
snippet: “It’s important for service members to understand the uncertainty inherent to LLMs," a GovAI research scholar warns.
fullText:
Military aircraft were already in the air this spring when U.S. officials made an alarming discovery: The intelligence driving an armed operation against a Chinese vessel had been hallucinated by an AI chatbot. The operation was aborted at the last minute, narrowly averting a potential conflict with China, CNN reported on Friday.

The episode underscores a growing concern among military officials and outside experts: As decision-makers lean more heavily on AI, the errors these systems produce can travel up the chain of command before being questioned.

The intelligence report, which circulated during the war with Iran, said the vessel was carrying components for a nuclear weapons program. 

The false intelligence originated with a Special Operations Command analyst who queried an AI chatbot to synthesize open source data with classified signals intelligence. The chatbot misidentified the ship’s cargo manifest. The analyst then used the tool a second time to format the erroneous findings into an official-looking summary, which was circulated across command channels.

The near-miss comes as the U.S. military races to integrate AI to accelerate decision-making and maintain its edge over China. The Pentagon has described AI as delivering a significant advantage in speeding up its kill chain so commanders can respond in the right time. But the same speed that makes AI attractive may also allow hallucinations with insufficient human oversight.

“It’s important for service members to understand the uncertainty inherent to LLMs,” said Jake Steckler, research scholar at GovAI and veteran U.S. Army officer, in a written response to TechCrunch. “But it’s especially critical for any decisions that could lead to use of force, like targeting, intelligence analysis, or operational planning. There are life and death consequences for those decisions.” 

Still, Steckler says, the incident should serve as a call to add more safeguards to AI, not a reason to avoid it. “These tools can be useful in the right contexts and with the right safeguards in place,” he said. “But prioritizing adoption speed over all else will likely lead to incidents that only make service members lose trust in these systems, which ultimately is only going to slow adoption.”

title: Manus seeks $4B valuation in new $500M fundraise as it resumes independent ops
snippet: Manus, which earlier this year had to break off a merger with Meta, is in discussions to raise $500M at a $4B valuation.
fullText:
Chinese AI startup Manus, which earlier this year had to break off a merger with Meta, is in discussions to raise $500 million at a $4 billion valuation now that it has resumed operations as an independent company, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing anonymous sources.

Potential investors in the round include IDG Capital, Boyu Capital, and battery maker Contemporary Amperex Technology, as well as existing backers Tencent, HSG, and ZhenFund, the Journal reported. Manus is also said to be considering a restructuring exercise to prepare for an IPO in Hong Kong.

Manus, which went viral following a demo of its AI agent last year, relocated its staff to Singapore in mid-2025 before announcing a $2 billion acquisition deal with Meta that December. The startup was said to be pulling in annual recurring revenue of over $100 million at the time. 

However, intensifying worries in China over losing AI talent and researchers to the West culminated in Beijing blocking the deal, citing potential violations of export controls and foreign investment rules. 

Manus has since been untangling itself from the American social media giant, and its early investors and backers have reportedly helped the company buy back its shares at a valuation of about $2 billion.

As part of its separation from Meta, the company told its users this August that they would have to export and back up their own data because it had to delete data generated following Meta’s acquisition to “comply with regulatory requirements in specific jurisdictions.” 

The company this month said it has resumed independent operations, and that its founding team will continue to lead it. 

Manus makes AI products and agents that are pretty similar to what companies like OpenAI, Lovable, and Replit offer. It offers a chatbot and vibe-coding tools to let users build apps and websites, create designs and presentations, generate video, and more.

Manus did not immediately return a request for comment.

title: Family offices are clamoring for AI investments
snippet: Whether it's a permanent shift or part of a familiar cycle is worth asking, though.
fullText:
For the wealthy families who manage their own money through a family office, the math right now is simple, according to Djoann Fal, a family office advisor and investor at the private wealth platform Atlas Capital in San Francisco.

A family office might want to put money into something like green energy for the long haul. But in the current environment, if a fund manager offers a deal that could triple an investor’s money over three years, and another deal could triple it in three months, the choice is easy. As Fal put it: If they have one deal that has the chance to make them 3x in three years, and another deal that could make them 3x in one quarter, “they’re just going to invest in the AI deal that does 3x in three months.”

It isn’t surprising that family offices want in on the action, given that everything around AI is so hot right now, from valuations to pricing to the potential for returns. A bigger shift is that they no longer necessarily want to invest the traditional way, through a venture capital fund manager. Instead, family offices are increasingly buying existing shares in a private company from existing shareholders, or making direct deals on their own. Both approaches get them exposure to the hottest companies without having to hand over control of their money to a fund manager for a decade.

“They have more dry powder to chase single-name deals,” Fal said, referring to family offices increasingly skipping so-called blind-pool fund commitments, where investors hand money to a fund manager without knowing in advance which companies it will be used to back. He said a new generation of family offices is emerging, too, with a higher appetite for risk than their predecessors. “Right now, the single names they want are the AI leaders,” he said.

They definitely have the money. Family offices were overseeing $5.5 trillion in wealth as of 2024, according to a Deloitte report published that same year, which projected that number to hit at least $9.5 trillion by 2030.

Underscoring Fal’s point, they want to pour more of it into riskier, but potentially more lucrative, assets, too. UBS’s 2026 Global Family Office Report, which surveyed 307 family offices worldwide with an average net worth of $2.7 billion, found that alternative investments — including private equity, venture capital, and private credit — now make up 42% of the average family office portfolio.

Whether that’s a permanent shift or part of a familiar cycle is worth asking, though. Family offices have been here before, more than once. Direct investment activity climbed steadily through the late 2010s, for example, then spiked hard in 2021, when direct deals hit 13% of the average family office portfolio, up from 9% in 2019, according to UBS’s own tracking at the time. 

Total family office deal activity peaked that year too, according to PwC’s Global Family Office Deals Study, at 17,460 deals worth roughly $1.05 trillion globally. Then it reversed just as fast, as rising interest rates and disappointing returns on some of those direct bets led many family offices to pull back. (Direct and M&A deal activity fell by 53% in just 18 months by late 2023, per PwC.) By the first half of 2025, overall family office deal volume had fallen to its lowest point in a decade.

Now it’s bouncing back, just as some would argue the market is overheated, and this time, family offices are writing bigger checks on fewer deals. Much of that activity is happening in the secondary market, which Fal calls the most “de-risked” asset in venture capital right now, since investors are often backing companies that already have customer traction and revenue proof. Angelina Hu, head of investor relations at Bridge Funding Global, put it another way: The secondary market lets family offices gain exposure to a private company without “taking exposure across 20-30 companies.”

“Family offices see the risk, but don’t want to miss the opportunity,” added Bruce K. Lee, founder of Keebeck Wealth Management.

That appetite is translating directly into Fal’s own business. He said he’s never raised this much money in his life — capital all earmarked for “AI things,” while clients who aren’t pouring money into AI are struggling to raise money at all. He said family offices currently have no problem paying “primary-style prices” for “secondary-stage risk,” even if it leaves them with “little room for outsized returns.”

Illustrating his point, Fal, whose clients primarily back climate-focused investments, said he spent the summer fielding interest from people looking to invest $50 million to $100 million into Anthropic through the secondary market. Anthropic stakes, alongside those of OpenAI, are among the most sought-after in the industry right now — what Emily Zheng, a senior VC analyst at PitchBook, described to TechCrunch as some of the “most contested real estate in venture.” Said Fal, “Even advisors with non-AI mandates are being pulled into transactions. That is where LP demand is.”

They see it as a comparatively safe investment in a volatile market. Indeed, a February report from J.P. Morgan Private Bank found that 65% of global family offices plan to “prioritize AI investments” despite concerns over inflated valuations and pricing. “Family offices are operating against a backdrop of geopolitical tensions, rising global debt levels, recession risk, and broader market uncertainty,” Maximilian Kunkel, chief investment officer of global family and institutional wealth at UBS Global Wealth Management, told TechCrunch.

Family offices clearly believe there is plenty of upside, too, in these investments. “AI is viewed as one of the most powerful long-term growth opportunities,” he continued. “The result is that investors are not choosing between resilience and growth. Instead, they are maintaining exposure to AI while diversifying across regions, currencies, and asset classes to manage concentration and macroeconomic risks.”

Whether that’s diverse enough is the big unanswered question. If the AI boom turns out to be a bubble that eventually bursts, the fallout won’t stay contained to AI stocks. As Lee put it, “everybody knows that if it goes under, the stock market’s going to have issues.” He said there are two types of investors right now: those sitting on the sideline, calling AI a bubble without owning any stock, and those who are anxious but effectively all-in. Some of his clients, he said, talk about AI being a bubble but don’t like to hear about ways to hedge against it. “We’re all addicted to returns,” he said. “That’s the sugar.”

title: FBI, Coast Guard boarded hacked oil tankers heading toward US coast
snippet: The feds are said to be investigating the compromise of the tankers' networks, which in one case interfered with one of the tanker's navigation and propulsion systems.
fullText:
Cybersecurity teams with the U.S. Coast Guard and the FBI boarded two U.S.-bound oil tankers last month after hackers reportedly compromised at least one of the ship’s networks and took control of its navigation, propulsion, and cargo systems.

According to a joint statement shared with TechCrunch, the agencies boarded the vessels in the Gulf of Mexico between August 21 and August 24 to “ensure integrity of the vessel’s operational and information technology systems following indications that the networks of both vessels were compromised.”

The Coast Guard released several photos of its staffers and FBI agents climbing aboard one of the vessels, which were shared with CBS News. The statement said that the captain, crew, and the on-shore staff of the vessel’s owner cooperated with the agencies.

The incident is an example of how shipping vessels, oil tankers, and the broader global logistics network can be targeted by hackers. Tankers often have complex networks sprawling the span of the vessel to aid with navigation, organizing cargo, and ensuring the regular running of services necessary with operating a massive ship.

A spokesperson for the Coast Guard did not comment beyond its emailed statement, including naming the vessels involved.

CBS News confirmed that one of the tankers is VL Prosperity, a 333-meter oil tanker that can hold over 2 million barrels of oil. According to VesselFinder, the tanker is currently located in the Gulf of Mexico.

Citing Iranian media, CBS said hackers compromised the ship on August 7 while traveling from Egypt to the United States and interfered with the ship’s speed and fuel systems. The tanker also lost communications for more than a day, per CBS.

It’s unclear who is behind the attacks, but CBS News said the U.S. is looking into whether Iran is behind the hack. Iran has been behind a multitude of hacks in recent months following the start of the U.S. and Israel-led war against Tehran, which killed Iran’s supreme leader in February. Iranian-backed hackers have since launched a destructive hack at medical device maker Stryker, hacked the mass transit system in Los Angeles, and compromised over a hundred water facilities across the United States in response to the widespread U.S. bombing of Iran. CISA has called the attacks “opportunistic” in nature.

The joint FBI-Coast Guard statement said that there were “no reports of operational disruptions, vessel instability, physical danger to crews, or environmental impacts.”

title: WhatsApp may soon let iPhone users add a third account
snippet: After recently letting iPhone users add a second account to the same app, WhatsApp is now working on expanding support to up to three accounts. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
After recently letting iPhone users add a second account to the same app, WhatsApp is now working on expanding support to up to three accounts. Here are the details.

WhatsApp to support up to three accounts

Last June, WhatsApp officially rolled out support for multiple accounts on iPhone, allowing users to add a second account to the same app.

The move came after the feature had spent several months in beta testing, giving users an alternative to relying on WhatsApp Business as a workaround for managing a second account.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, the app appears to be working on expanding the feature to let users switch between up to three accounts without logging out.

Image: WABetaInfo

From WABetaInfo:

The attached image shows the account selector when multi-account supports up to three profiles. The left screen shows the option to add a second account at the bottom of the interface. The right screen shows the interface when users log into their third profile. The layout is the same as before, so accounts appear with their name, profile photo, and phone number, and the active one has a green checkmark. When this feature becomes available, users will see the “Add account” option even when they have two active profiles in the same app. Note that WhatsApp may support even more than three accounts in the future.

The report adds that each account will keep its own chat history, notifications, privacy settings, backups, and media.

WABetaInfo notes that while two accounts may be enough for many users, the feature could come in handy for those who have different combinations of work and personal phone numbers.

That said, the feature is still under development and isn’t available to beta testers yet, suggesting there may still be some time before a wider rollout.

title: Apple rolls out first Release Candidates for macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1
snippet: After releasing macOS 27.2 beta 1 earlier today, Apple is now rolling out the first RCs of macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1. Here are the details. more…
fullText:

RCs for macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 now available

title: AI Firms Knew Chatbots Were an ‘Existential Threat’ to Journalists, Court Docs Show
snippet: A Microsoft executive called OpenAI’s use of publishers’ material “the largest theft of labor in human history.”
fullText:
AI companies used vast troves of published text to train their large language models, and executives at those firms were aware that doing so constituted a theft of copyrighted materials, according to comments cited by news publishers in a court filing that was unredacted this week.

The brief was initially filed earlier this month in a court proceeding that brings together several related copyright infringement cases against ChatGPT maker OpenAI and its partner Microsoft, including lawsuits brought by The New York Times and by Ziff Davis, which owns CNET.

Microsoft’s director of applied science, Brent Hecht, called it “an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions” and maybe the “largest theft of labor in human history,” according to the publishers’ filing. The full exhibits showing the context of the quotes in the filing remain under seal.

The comments cited by publishers appear to undercut the argument by AI companies that the use of copyrighted material was legally protected as fair use. Under this legal doctrine, use of copyrighted material is protected depending on how it’s used, the nature of the work, how much of it was used and the effect of the use on the market for that work. 

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said under oath that conversations with chatbots gave information “right there on the website on the AI platform versus needing to go to the underlying source,” like the website of a publisher that reported the information, according to the filing. Similarly, an OpenAI executive wrote that publishers faced an “existential threat” from products like the company’s chatbot.

The publishers’ brief also describes steps AI developers took to evade paywalls, like that for The New York Times. It describes how an OpenAI employee told the company’s president, Greg Brockman, about “a hack to get around nytimes paywall,” to which Brockman replied, “ah nice.” 

At the same time, the filing says Nadella testified that anything behind a paywall “should be licensed by anyone who wants to use it” for AI development and that if he had been aware OpenAI had trained on paywalled content, he would have required OpenAI to retrain its models. 

In a statement provided to CNET, a Microsoft spokesperson said that Hecht’s comments “reflect one employee’s perspectives” and that the company’s position is in its court filings, which “explain why these transformative uses are consistent with copyright law and why Copilot is not a substitute for publishers’ journalism.”

Nadella’s comments addressed changes in how people consume information and are “perfectly consistent” with the company’s legal position, the spokesperson said. “Those observations should not be confused with conclusions about copyright questions before the Court, which Microsoft addresses in its filings.”

In its own brief in the case, Microsoft said the use of published content to train LLMs was significantly transformative. “Copyright law does not permit rightsholders to block transformative technologies like LLMs; it encourages such uses on the expectation that rightsholders will adapt and the public will be better off for it,” the company argued.

Representatives for OpenAI and Ziff Davis did not immediately respond to requests for comment. 

LLMs are trained on as much published content as developers can get their hands on, and the litigation over copyright — including related cases from book authors — could have a significant impact on both AI companies and media outlets. Publishers argue AI companies should have to pay to license the content they use, while the tech companies say doing so is unnecessary and burdensome to the development of more capable AI. The Trump administration weighed in on the case earlier this month with a statement arguing a licensing requirement would impede American AI development in a race with China. 

OpenAI and Microsoft employees were also aware that their chatbots’ ability to find, copy, summarize and sometimes regurgitate content from publishers was keeping readers from visiting the sites of news organizations, the publishers argue. 

“Defendants’ own experts acknowledge that grounded LLMs exploit their sources rather than promote them like search uses that have been deemed fair use,” the publishers’ filing states.

title: Apple releases first iOS 27.2 developer beta for iPhone
snippet: Apple has released the first iOS 27.2 developer beta for iPhone. The update follows the release of iOS 27 to everyone on Monday. It also leaps over iOS 27.1, which Apple has shown as an iPhone Duo-focused release. more…
fullText:
Apple has released the first iOS 27.2 developer beta for iPhone. The update follows the release of iOS 27 to everyone on Monday. It also leaps over iOS 27.1, which Apple has shown as an iPhone Duo-focused release. 

iOS 27.2 beta 1 arrives before iOS 27.1 beta

Today’s beta release follows the official launch of iOS 27 on September 14. The new version comes as a sizable 22GB update.

Apple has already detailed how the iOS 27.1 SDK will let developers take full advantage of the iPhone Duo display. You can see how apps will appear on iPhone Duo based on which iOS version they target here.

But today’s iOS 27.2 developer beta 1 release skips over iOS 27.1 for now.

Apple presumably wants to save iPhone Duo-specific code until closer to the new hardware’s release in October. However, developers will still need to prepare their apps for the new device. Apple has said to expect the tools for this to be ready by the end of September.

Apple has already pointed to other changes for all iPhones coming next month. This includes the redesigned Apple Health app as well as expanded Siri AI support.

“A more capable and conversational assistant with personal context understanding, broad world knowledge, onscreen awareness, and even more systemwide app actions, Siri AI is now rolling out as a beta in English, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish coming in October,” Apple confirmed this week.

This likely gives us an idea of when to expect the official release.

We’ll know more about what Apple has included in this first release once we have it running.

We’ll cover new features and other changes in a separate roundup as we explore today’s new beta update. Stay tuned for our ongoing iOS 27.2 beta coverage.

title: iCloud+ subscribers just got new benefits in iOS 27
snippet: iOS 27 launched this week, and it includes several new Apple Intelligence-related benefits for iCloud+ subscribers. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 launched this week, and it includes several new Apple Intelligence-related benefits for iCloud+ subscribers.

iCloud+ gives iOS 27 users higher AI usage limits, plus new Home features

There are a variety of new Apple Intelligence features that just arrived in iOS 27, many of which you can read about here.

As part of Apple overhauling its AI offerings, though, the company shared that certain features come with daily usage limits. That’s because they rely on “powerful server models.”

While all of these features are available free for users, iCloud+ subscribers gain the benefit of higher usage limits in iOS 27.

Per Apple’s press release:

Some Apple Intelligence features, including image generation, have daily usage limits because they rely on powerful server models. Increased access is available with most iCloud+ subscription plans, which also include Apple Intelligence support for compatible Home cameras.

By saying “with most iCloud+ subscription plans,” presumably Apple is excluding the cheapest $0.99/month plan. But so far we haven’t gotten confirmation of specifics.

However, if you’re using any of the other iCloud+ tiers, or are an Apple One subscriber, iOS 27 provides more leeway when using certain advanced AI features—such as image generation, for example.

Additionally, the Home app in iOS 27 has some great AI features for iCloud+ subscribers too via upgrades to HomeKit Secure Video.

With the new features and iCloud+, your compatible home camera can get AI video descriptions, let you search clips, and surface noteworthy clips automatically.

It’s unrelated to iOS 27, but this week Apple also expanded iCloud+ to include free Apple TV and Apple Arcade in much of the world outside the US.

fullText:
Stevie Bonifield

 

is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

A team of three independent security researchers at Hacktron says it took less than 72 hours for them to hack into OpenAI employee accounts using Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 and 5, The Wall Street Journal reports. They were able to access OpenAI’s GitHub repository, called “Monorepo,” which reportedly contains “OpenAI’s algorithmic secrets,” according to The Wall Street Journal’s sources.

They stopped short of accessing internal code in Monorepo themselves, but sent a pull request from an employee’s Codex account to prove they gained access. They were able to get in through Discourse, the third-party service that hosts OpenAI’s community forums, by exploiting an issue with the system it uses to process HEIF images. According to Hacktron, Claude Opus 5 launched in the evening on July 24th, and by 10AM the next day they had used it to achieve RCE on Discourse Cloud and accessed OpenAI’s instance.

Their HEIF Heist project took “only one or two days” to adapt to different companies, including OpenAI, Slack, Meta, GitHub Ent, Rails, Next.js, ImageMagick, and others, using less than $3,000 in tokens, and to their knowledge, was only detected by one target, Shopify. The vulnerabilities Hacktron reported to Discourse and OpenAI have since been fixed, and Hacktron says OpenAI paid it $6,500 for finding the bug, but as Hacktron CTO Mohan Pedhapati said to the WSJ, “I don’t think we are as strong as Chinese threat actors… We’re just three guys with Claude and Codex subscriptions.”

title: iOS 27.2 will help users move data and settings from an old app to its replacement
snippet: Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to move their data and settings from an existing app to its designated replacement. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will be able to offer users a way to move their data and settings from an existing app to its designated replacement. Here are the details.

iOS to make app replacement easier

While uncommon, developers occasionally retire an existing app and launch a new one in its place, requiring users to move over to a separate app.

Even though most developers try to make that transition as seamless as possible, migrating can still require some work from the user, particularly when it involves data that isn’t stored in the cloud.

With iOS 27.2, Apple will address this with a new system-managed migration flow that can move an app’s data and supported settings to its designated replacement before deleting the old app.

Based on existing code in iOS 27.2 beta 1, users will be presented with an alert that says:

The developer recommends moving your existing “%1$@” app data and settings to the new “%2$@” app.

iPhone can do this for you now, before you start using your new app. Afterwards, the old app will be deleted from this iPhone.

Users will then be able to choose either “Move App Data and Settings” or “Don’t Move Anything.” If the user rejects the migration, iOS will present a second confirmation warning that some preferences, including notification and location settings, may need to be configured again.

To be clear, the feature appears to be limited to cases where a developer replaces one of its own apps with a designated successor, rather than migrating data between apps from different developers.

Based on the current implementation, iOS can migrate a range of system-level settings and permissions, including:

Privacy, location, and Health authorization decisions

Notification settings, including accessory notification settings

Per-app Do Not Disturb and Focus settings

App locking and protection settings

CarPlay icon order and compatible widget layouts

Live Activities and accessory Live Activities

Access to associated accessories

LaunchServices preferences, fonts, capture-related defaults, telephony data, and Secure Element services

We will keep an eye out for changes to this framework during the iOS 27.2 beta cycle and report back if we learn more about how developers will be able to implement it.

title: Here are 100+ things Siri AI can do on your iPhone
snippet: iOS 27 launched this week with the all-new Siri AI. David Pogue put the new Siri to the test by trying 125 requests, here’s how it went. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 launched this week with the all-new Siri AI. David Pogue put the new Siri to the test by trying 125 requests, here’s how it went.

iOS 27’s new Siri AI impresses David Pogue following 125 tests

Siri has been baked into the iPhone for nearly 15 years. But during that time, many Apple users have grown accustomed to only depending on Siri for certain supported tasks.

For example, I’ve long relied on Siri to create reminders, start timers, play Apple Music, and when driving I’ll use it to send messages. Outside of those few limited tasks though, Siri’s shortcomings have trained me to not rely on it.

But iOS 27’s new Siri AI is a huge upgrade that can do so much more than ever before. It might just take some time to adjust to it being your go-to, though.

That’s why I found David Pogue’s new Substack post so helpful. Titled “125 Tests of the New AI Siri,” Pogue lists out over 100 prompts he’s tried with Siri AI and details how the assistant did.

Here are a few examples that stood out to me:

28. What are people waiting on me for? (Generates list from Mail, Messages, and Reminders. Incredible. Everything I did for this column was supposed to be for testing purposes only, but this one actually found stuff I’d forgotten I was supposed to do!) […]

30. (Running late to a party:) What’s the apartment number!? (“The apartment number for the Bynum party tonight is 10-F.” Note: I never said what party or what day!) […]

46. Delete all my alarms. (“Do you want to delete 38 alarms in Clock?” Tap to confirm.)

With almost every one of the 125 tests, Siri succeeded. And among the few failures, such as sending a Venmo payment, Siri AI will likely perform better after third parties update their apps for iOS 27 and Siri AI compatibility. 

You can read the full list of 125 Siri AI examples here on Pogue’s Substack.

How has Siri been running for you in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.

title: iOS 27.2 introduces Apple Health app overhaul, here’s what’s new
snippet: Today Apple released iOS 27.2 beta 1, skipping over 27.1 entirely in the testing cycle. And among other changes, the new iOS 27.2 update includes the previously announced all-new Health app. more…
fullText:
Today Apple released iOS 27.2 beta 1, skipping over 27.1 entirely in the testing cycle. And among other changes, the new iOS 27.2 update includes the previously announced all-new Health app.

All-new Apple Health app debuts in iOS 27.2 beta 1

Last week during its September event, Apple unveiled an all-new Health app that would be coming to iPhone later this year.

Now today, beta testers have received the first access to the Health app redesign via iOS 27.2 beta 1.

When Apple introduced the new Health app, it emphasized how Apple Intelligence would be used to help users better understand their health. Here’s what the company said:

The Health app has been redesigned to dynamically respond to a user’s data using Apple Intelligence, with a new Insights tab that surfaces timely health information and a new Longevity tab that analyzes a user’s longitudinal health data for deeper insights. The Longevity tab includes Health Age, an Apple Watch feature that shows users how certain metrics are tracking relative to their actual age. The Health app also includes movement evaluations that measure flexibility, strength, balance, and more using vision-based AI models on iPhone and heart rate data from Apple Watch.

Now today with iOS 27.2 beta 1, the new Insights tab and Longevity tab are both available for testing if you’re a developer.

Because the new Health app relies on Apple Intelligence, you’ll need an AI-compatible iPhone to try it out. Certain features require a paired Apple Watch too. And your device must be set to US English.

So if your iPhone is less powerful than an iPhone 15 Pro, or you don’t have a compatible Apple Watch, the Health app upgrades will be missing. But for everyone else, iOS 27.2 provides a first glimpse at Apple’s expanded vision for the Health app.

Note: Apple says additional Health features will roll out in future betas, like the ability to order labs from Quest and personalized recommendations. Also, despite its availability in the beta, Apple says the new Health app won’t actually ship in iOS 27.2 but instead is coming later in the year.

title: iPhone 18 Pro Max still uses a Qualcomm modem in the US, teardown confirms
snippet: TechInsights has published one of the first in-depth iPhone 18 Pro Max teardowns. Most notably, the teardown confirms that the iPhone 18 Pro Max sold in the United States still uses a Qualcomm modem. more…
fullText:
TechInsights has published one of the first in-depth iPhone 18 Pro Max teardowns. Most notably, the teardown confirms that the iPhone 18 Pro Max sold in the United States still uses a Qualcomm modem.

On its tech specs website, Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro uses the Apple C2 cellular modem. In every country other than the United States, Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro Max also uses its C2 cellular modem.

The company, however, doesn’t specify which modem the U.S. variant of the iPhone 18 Pro Max uses. Speculation suggested the iPhone 18 Pro Max used a Qualcomm modem, and this teardown confirms it.

According to the TechInsights teardown, the iPhone 18 Pro Max variant sold in the United States uses the Qualcomm Snapdragon X80 modem. This is the same modem used worldwide in the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 17 Pro Max.

So, to recap, here’s how Apple’s transition to its own in-house modem technology has played out in the United States specifically:

iPhone 16 / 16 Plus / 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max: Qualcomm Snapdragon X71

iPhone 16e: Apple C1

iPhone 17 / 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max: Qualcomm X80

iPhone Air: Apple C1X

iPhone 17e: Apple C1X

iPhone 18 Pro: Apple C2

iPhone 18 Pro Max: Qualcomm X80

iPhone Duo: Apple C2

Apple touts that the C2 brings “AI-powered improvements to cellular quality and reliability.” In comparison to the C1X, Apple says the C2 delivers “meaningfully faster uploads when compared to C1X while consuming 15 percent less energy.” The C2 modem also supports mmWave 5G, unlike the C1 and C1X.

It seems clear to me that Apple has caught up to Qualcomm, now that the C2 supports mmWave 5G connectivity. Apple’s C-series modems have always been more power-efficient than Qualcomm’s (which, I’d wager, is something most people care more about than raw download and upload speeds).

Apple hasn’t said why the iPhone 18 Pro Max still uses a Qualcomm modem. The likely explanation, though, is that the decision is purely contractual, and Apple will ditch Qualcomm once and for all as soon as it can.

title: Samsung starts rolling out Android 17 with One UI 9, confirms initial list of Galaxy devices
snippet: After months in beta, Samsung is now rolling out One UI 9, based on Android 17, to select Galaxy devices. more…
fullText:
After months in beta, Samsung is now rolling out One UI 9, based on Android 17, to select Galaxy devices.

Confirmed in a newsroom post, Samsung has officially started rolling out its One UI 9 update. This is an Android 17-based update and first debuted on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series and Flip 8 in July.

As of today, only the Galaxy S26 series – S26, S26+, and S26 Ultra – will start getting the stable update. This comes after around four months in beta, and signals that a wider rollout is likely just a few weeks away. Samsung says the update will “gradually roll out to other Galaxy devices.”

What’s new in One UI 9? Samsung’s Android 17 update has a few notable changes including:

	

My FanCam: Automatic video tracking & reframing of a subject

Generative and Editable Cards on Now Brief

Warranty and Care details in Settings menu

More Galaxy AI features: Now Nudge, Creative Studio, Interpreter, Document Scan, Voice Recorder

Privacy & security features: Security Brief, Privacy Alerts, Scam Detection

In a footnote around Privacy Alerts, Samsung reveals at least a partial list of Galaxy devices that will be getting Android 17 including:

Galaxy S26/S26 Ultra

Galaxy S25/S25 FE

Galaxy S24/S24 FE

title: Apple planning to sell AI servers powered by M8 Ultra chips, says report
snippet: Apple is working on plans to make enterprise servers powered by M8 Ultra chips, according to a new report. The report specifically says that the company plans to offer the AI-focused servers for sale, not just use them internally. Two versions are said to be in development, with Apple considering incorporating Nvidia networking tech in the machines … more…
fullText:
Apple is working on plans to make enterprise servers powered by M8 Ultra chips, according to a new report. The report specifically says that the company plans to offer the AI-focused servers for sale, not just use them internally.

Two versions are said to be in development, with Apple considering incorporating Nvidia networking tech in the machines … 

The Information reports that plans have not yet been finalized and that the servers are not expected to go on sale until 2029.

Apple has been developing the server with plans to sell it to AI developers, other businesses and governments, the people said. The product under consideration would come in two versions—a smaller one with two of Apple’s planned M8 Ultra chips clustered together, and a bigger one with four M8 Ultra chips.

Apple has considered connecting the M8 chips in the server using an Nvidia set of products called NVLink Fusion, which includes switches, chiplets and software that help chips communicate with each other in data centers.

Apple is said to have been working on the project for around a year, with CEO John Ternus in favor.

9to5Mac’s Take

While 2029 is some way off, and the report acknowledges that the project could be canceled before then, it does make a great deal of sense. People are already using clusters of Mac Studios to run AI models locally, so it seems clear there would be a market for more powerful Apple servers. The only question is whether this is a big enough priority for Apple to say yes to launching it.

title: In India, the new iPhone can arrive faster than a pizza
snippet: Availability of Apple's iPhone 18 Pro series turned patchy within hours of its debut on India's quick-commerce apps.
fullText:
For some iPhone buyers in India, getting Apple’s brand-new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max did not require lining up outside a store or waiting days for delivery. They needed only a few taps on a quick-commerce app to get one delivered to their doorstep in about 10 minutes.

Blinkit, Zepto, Swiggy’s Instamart, and BigBasket — platforms best known in India for delivering groceries and everyday essentials in minutes — began offering the new Pro models as they went on sale in the country on Friday. The phones are, however, also available through Apple’s usual sales channels, including its stores, authorized retailers, and online marketplaces.

Putting a new iPhone on a 10-minute delivery app is not entirely new in India. Quick-commerce platforms have offered Apple’s latest devices on launch day previously as well, as they have steadily expanded beyond groceries into categories including electronics, beauty products, and fashion.

However, the market behind those deliveries is growing rapidly. India’s quick-commerce sector reached about $9 billion in the first half of 2026, per a recent report by Redseer Strategy Consultants, with the number of monthly users rising to more than 60 million from 8 million three years ago. Google and Deloitte separately estimate the market could reach $50 billion by 2030, with non-food products such as electronics, fashion, and beauty accounting for 45% of spending.

There were signs of strong demand on launch day. BigBasket said it delivered more than 300 iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max units in the first hour of sales. Instamart told TechCrunch that Bengaluru led the iPhone 18 Pro-series orders on its platform, followed by Delhi. The Burgundy 256 GB iPhone 18 Pro was Instamart’s most popular variant, accounting for nearly a third of its sales.

Nonetheless, within hours of launch, availability of the new iPhones became patchy. TechCrunch found the iPhone 18 Pro models sold out on some quick-commerce platforms and in some locations, while they remained available for delivery elsewhere in cities including Delhi and Bengaluru.

Tarun Pathak, research director at Counterpoint Research, said the launch-day deliveries showed that quick commerce could work as a channel for premium smartphones in India’s biggest cities, even though volumes remain small compared with overall iPhone sales.

The ability to fulfill high-value smartphone orders provides an “early proof of concept,” Pathak told TechCrunch. “The key question is whether this launch-driven demand can translate into regular smartphone purchases through quick-commerce platforms.”

Navkendar Singh, associate vice president at IDC, said India stood out globally for this kind of quick-commerce delivery and was particularly suited to such purchases because consumers in major cities had built trust in the platforms by using them regularly for everyday purchases. Official tie-ups between brands and the platforms also gave consumers greater confidence in buying expensive products through them, he told TechCrunch.

For a product like the iPhone, the appeal also comes down to “instant gratification,” Singh said, allowing buyers to avoid queues outside stores or waiting several days for an online order to arrive. Still, he cautioned that quick commerce was not yet a significant sales channel for smartphones. Its role around new iPhone releases is largely a “launch-day marketing phenomenon” that “creates good noise around the launch,” he said.

title: iOS 27.2 lets developers use an alternative App Tracking Transparency prompt in the EU
snippet: Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will have the option to use an alternative App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the EU, as part of Apple’s recent deal with the bloc. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Starting with iOS 27.2, developers will have the option to use an alternative App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the EU, as part of Apple’s recent deal with the bloc. Here are the details.

New prompt is mandatory in select European countries

A few weeks ago, Apple confirmed it would comply with “fairer” App Tracking Transparency rules in the EU, following an investigation by Germany’s Federal Cartel Office.

The deal concluded a years-long antitrust probe into whether Apple’s ATT rules unfairly disadvantaged third-party apps compared with its own services. Apple has always denied the allegations, claiming that it applies the same strict privacy principles to its own apps from the ground up. German regulators, however, remained unconvinced.

As a result, Apple agreed to eight changes in the ATT framework in Europe, and you can read more about that here.

That said, Apple confirmed today that iOS 27 will let developers choose whether they want to “use an alternative version of the App Tracking Transparency system prompt in the EU,” and added that “due to legal requirements, only the alternative version of the system prompt is available for apps distributed in Germany, France, Italy, Poland, and Romania.”

In an update to the “User privacy and data use” developer support page, Apple elaborates on the alternative version of this system prompt:

The alternative version of the App Tracking Transparency system prompt has modified formatting and language and provides you the option to use a text button labeled “Additional Information.” This allows you to surface additional information about your request to link user or device data collected from your app with user or device data collected from other companies’ apps, websites, or offline properties for targeted advertising or advertising measurement purposes, or to share user or device data with a data broker.

The company adds that EU developers will also be able to re-prompt users one year after their previous ATT choice, regardless of whether they initially accepted or declined tracking.

title: Anthropic is operating a lab that conducts biology experiments
snippet: AI leaders have been promising that AI is the key to curing human disease. Anthropic researchers have also been warning that AI might kill us all.
fullText:
Anthropic has a wet biology lab in the Bay Area where it can use its AI models to run physical experiments, it has confirmed to TechCrunch.

AI leaders have been promising that AI is the key to curing human disease. Dario Amodei opined just last week: “I believe that AI could cure most major diseases in the next 5–10 years.” To do that, an LLM would have to have methods to test its theories in real life.

“We believe that to do biology, the final test is still, and will be for a while, in real lab work,” Anthropic’s head of life sciences, Eric Kauderer-Abrams, told Reuters. “We absolutely are doing that today.” He added that the lab operates like most biotech labs: Anthropic conducts some research there while also working with external partners.

This news probably shouldn’t be shocking. Anthropic bought Coefficient Bio, a stealth AI biotech, in April.

While Anthropic declined to give specifics on what the wet lab is working on, it did say the main focus was fundamental biology, not drug discovery.

Anthropic doesn’t want to give the appearance of competing with the pharma industry, where it has numerous major customers and partners (e.g., it just announced a deal to work with Novo Nordisk on joint drug discovery). Anthropic has already faced backlash for launching products perceived to compete with those of its customers.

To that end, Anthropic also launched a Life Sciences Verification Program this week, to give vetted bio researchers access to its most powerful models. It has also published recent reports on some of the research it’s doing to support drug discovery. This includes one report on accelerating protein design and one on uplifting bimolecular modeling.

But the world is still reeling from the resignation of Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who warned that “the people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade.” Anthropic’s own alignment lead gave the odds at greater than 10% that AI could exterminate humanity within the next decade.

The fervor has grown so intense that CEO Dario Amodei published a post last weekend calling on the industry to slow down and institute self-regulation. He has repeatedly called bioterrorism one of AI’s biggest risks.

The juxtaposition of these dire warnings and the wet lab has not gone unnoticed in the tech industry. As investor and AI coding startup founder Chamath Palihapitiya posted on X, somewhat tongue in cheek: “The group behind such hits as: ‘We’re All Going To Die’ and ‘Regulate Me Now’ are building a wet lab in SF. I do not recommend this.”

fullText:

Back up your Mac

title: Philips Hue Bridge Pro is now $139, with even bigger price hikes globally
snippet: The Philips Hue Bridge Pro is a massive functional upgrade for your smart home lighting, but it now comes at a much higher cost, with price hikes now in effect around the globe. more…
fullText:
The Philips Hue Bridge Pro is a massive functional upgrade for your smart home lighting, but it now comes at a much higher cost, with price hikes now in effect around the globe.

In the US, Philips Hue launched its Bridge Pro last year at $99. Now, that price has jumped up to $139 across the Hue Shop, Amazon, and other retailers. It’s a price hike of roughly 40% and appears to have kicked in around mid-late August.

That’s almost certainly due to the rising costs of memory, as Bridge Pro has 8GB of RAM.

But the price hikes are even worse in other regions. Hue Blog reports that the price has jumped from an initial cost of €89 to €149 now. And that price hike appears to have just kicked in throughout Europe, with some retailers not yet showing the updated pricing. The report also notes that European prices on several other Hue products have gone up by around €10-20 each, including the Hue Essential bulb 4-pack going from €59 to €69.

title: OmniFocus adds Siri AI support as Omni Group updates its apps for iOS 27, macOS 27, more
snippet: Unsurprisingly, the Omni Group worked all summer to get its suite of apps ready for Apple’s 2027 system updates from day one. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
Unsurprisingly, the Omni Group worked all summer to get its suite of apps ready for Apple’s 2027 system updates from day one. Here’s what’s new.

OmniGroup updates its suite of apps for Apple’s 2027 system releases

As the Omni Group’s CEO, Ken Case shared in a fun blog post titled “Hey Siri, We’re Ready!” the teams behind OmniGraffle, OmniOutliner, OmniPlan, and OmniFocus worked hard to get all of the company’s apps “ready for all of Apple’s platform updates, compatible universally across the board.”

Here’s Case:

This is no small juggling act, with OmniGraffle supporting three platforms, OmniOutliner and OmniPlan supporting four platforms, and OmniFocus supporting five platforms—especially while we’re simultaneously pushing forward on new major features of our own for each product.

Chief among the updates is OmniFocus 4.9, which is fully compatible with macOS 27 Golden Gate, iOS 27, iPadOS 27, watchOS 27, and visionOS 27. That includes Siri AI support, optional Apple Intelligence-powered date parsing, “a range of new and updated App Intents exposed as Shortcuts actions,” and design refinements to better match Apple’s 2027 system updates.

OmniFocus users can now ask Siri to assign and edit due dates, flags, notes, and even repeat schedules. The app can also take advantage of broader Siri AI capabilities, such as onscreen awareness and Visual Intelligence, to help users get things into OmniFocus more quickly:

For example, you can pick up a note with hand-written action items and ask Siri to add those items to OmniFocus. Or you can take a picture of a whiteboard and ask Siri to do things with that input.

Siri AI can now also leverage the user’s personal context, which in practice means it can answer questions based on the user’s OmniFocus database, summarize actions, suggest items to work on, turn follow-up items from meeting notes into reminders, and more.

Other tidbits from the Omni Group’s round of updates this week include:

OmniOutliner 6.3 has also been updated with Liquid Glass refinements across Apple’s platforms.

OmniFocus and OmniOutliner now include a new API that lets users and tools search the Omni Automation API, which should make it easier to pull up the documentation needed to write scripts.

The Omni Group says that work is also part of its effort toward implementing the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Finally, Case also noted that, following last week’s iPhone Duo announcement, the team is already working to get its apps ready for the foldable’s launch.

title: What Hollywood thinks about existential AI warnings
snippet: As the tech sector sounds alarms about AI's potential to destroy humanity, entertainment labor groups are urging the public to stay focused on what's already happening. The Verge reached out to Disney, Netflix, Amazon, Lionsgate, and other studios who have started using AI, as well film startups focused on bringing generative AI into the mainstream to ask for their reaction to the recent warnings surrounding the technology. None have responded to our request for comment. The Screen Actors Guild - American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) and Writers Guild of America East (WGAE) did, however. The AI tools used in entert … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
As the tech sector sounds alarms about AI’s potential to destroy humanity, entertainment labor groups are urging the public to stay focused on what’s already happening. The Verge reached out to Disney, Netflix, Amazon, Lionsgate, and other studios who have started using AI, as well film startups focused on bringing generative AI into the mainstream to ask for their reaction to the recent warnings surrounding the technology. None have responded to our request for comment. The Screen Actors Guild – American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) and Writers Guild of America East (WGAE) did, however.

The AI tools used in entertainment production differ from the AI systems that have sparked a recent round of whistleblowing and apocalyptic declarations. They do not seem to be as existentially dangerous as the AI systems that drove former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon to quit his job and prompted Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger to insist that the technology could “kill all humans” at some point “within the next decade.”

But despite the differences between entertainment-focused AI and the models developed by Anthropic and OpenAI, AI models that generate digital facsimiles of actors and attempt to replicate traditional filmmaking tools pose a threat to some human jobs. Similar to the way that the Hollywood unions advocated for protections and increased oversight around AI’s use during the 2023 strikes, Coxon’s Anthropic exit has inspired a wave of AI researchers to speak out in favor of stronger safety protocols. The heads of major AI companies including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and X have also called for an industry-wide slowdown on the technology’s development. While president Donald Trump has dismissed these concerns as overreactions, some other US politicians have felt pressured to take legislative action. Hollywood unions’ fight for strict rules around gen AI’s use did not stop the entertainment industry from embracing AI, but they have given Hollywood’s laborers a way to fight back in instances when they feel that AI tools are being used to harm them.

When I recently spoke with the Screen Actors Guild – American Federation of Television and Radio Artists’ (SAG-AFTRA) chief negotiator Duncan Crabtree Ireland, he told me that the union recognized early on how AI could impact its members’ livelihoods. Most people might not have been familiar with the idea of studios completely replacing human actors with digital replicas, but SAG-AFTRA understood that it had an opportunity to shape public opinion about AI in Hollywood by “speaking out about it at the earliest possible point we could.”

“We bargained for and achieved enforceable, meaningful guardrails around how this technology can be implemented by the major employers in our industry,” Crabtree-Ireland explained. “That doesn’t include companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google directly, but it does encompass all of the companies who have built up businesses around the creation of professional level entertainment content in the United States.”

Though Crabtree-Ireland believes we “should be concerned about the broader societal and social implications of AI,” he also thinks that some of the warnings about the technology being an extinction-level threat could potentially be hyperbole and overblown. Doomerism has become one of the more common ways that AI companies generate buzz around their products, but the fact that Coxon left Anthropic to sound the alarm has given Crabtree-Ireland pause. Hearing the message from “the CEOs of these companies or the billionaires who’ve made their billions off of doing the exact thing that they’re now warning us might not be good,” has left him unsure “what to trust or what to believe.” But he acknowledged that Coxon was able to achieve “traction with the public.”

“The recklessness of the tech oligarchs pushing AI on our society has been matched only by their rampant dishonesty.”

Getting people to believe that SAG-AFTRA’s fears about AI should be taken seriously was one of the union’s major goals when its members voted to strike. The key to doing that, Crabtree-Ireland told me, was leading the strike with a focused message that clearly laid out to the public what was at stake and steps that could be taken to prevent worst case scenarios. If not for that, Crabtree-Ireland thinks that the Alliance of Motion Picture and Television Producers (AMPTP) might not have agreed to some of the union’s demands like requiring that studios gain permission and compensate actors for the use of their AI-generated replicas. “If that principle hadn’t been established, I think the economic incentive to use replication and to replace human performances would have been much stronger” and “would have resulted in a much greater and faster adoption of digital replication.” Had the protections not been codified, Crabtree-Ireland is confident that entertainment workers would be in a much more dire position now.

Writers Guild of America East (WGAE) executive director Sam Wheeler was much more pointed in his condemnation of the “tech oligarchs pushing AI on our society” whose recklessness “has been matched only by their rampant dishonesty.” But while Wheeler finds it hard to take AI companies’ warnings at face value, he noted that the WGAE “has long warned that unregulated artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to workers, to our democracy, and to the world.”

“Guild members have bargained meaningful AI protections into their contracts; in 2023 WGA members spent 148 days on strike before the film and television studios agreed to real safeguards for film and television writers,” Wheeler said. “But collective bargaining is not a replacement for government regulation, and we are grateful to states like New York that continue to enact meaningful regulations in the absence of federal action.”

Wheeler listed the disempowerment of workers, the degradation of the internet, the spread of disinformation, and increasing energy costs as some of the tangible societal harms AI has exacerbated. He urged policymakers not to be distracted by AI companies’ claims of ushering in an apocalypse because the real issue at hand is people behaving irresponsibly.

“These harms are the result of decisions made by human beings,” Wheeler insisted. “The WGAE believes that addressing those concrete harms and holding AI companies and their executives liable for the destruction their products cause is the surest way to safeguard against any worst-case scenarios.”

title: Ulysses gets Siri AI support, customizable toolbars, project templates, more
snippet: Following the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27, Ulysses was updated with Siri AI support, a refreshed interface, customizable toolbars, project templates, and more. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Following the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27, Ulysses was updated with Siri AI support, a refreshed interface, customizable toolbars, project templates, and more. Here are the details.

Ulysses adds support for Siri AI

My first Ulysses note dates back to December 2016. Since then, I’ve used the app on my Mac nearly every single day.

Whether I’m drafting an email, putting together podcast show notes, or writing a story for 9to5Mac and beyond, if it involves typing, I start in Ulysses.

Over the past 10 years, it’s been interesting to watch Ulysses evolve, embracing new workflows and adapting to users’ needs without losing what makes it so great, at least for me: a plain writing app with excellent Markdown support and no distractions.

In keeping with that approach, Ulysses was updated with support for iOS 27 and macOS 27. The update introduces Siri AI support (except for users in the EU), including onscreen awareness and a dedicated macOS toolbar button that brings up the new Siri AI interface for writing, rewriting, proofreading, and otherwise working with text.

And speaking of the app’s toolbar, Ulysses now lets users fully customize it, with navigation buttons, blocks, spaces, suggestions, and more.

The update also includes new group icons with much-requested pictograms, and improves accessibility support “when editing filter conditions and group icons.”

Finally, in addition to visual tweaks that better match the look of iOS 27 and macOS 27, the update adds project templates. Here’s Ulysses:

When creating a new project, you can now select a template, so projects start with a couple of dummy groups and sheets.

title: Tilly Norwood’s press tour is going about as well as you’d expect for an AI
snippet: In one particularly odd interview, Norwood seems to malfunction and begin speaking Chinese.
fullText:
Tilly Norwood, an AI-generated “actress,” is having a rough time on its first press tour. The production company that created it, Particle6 Group, has made it available for 75 simultaneous interviews with journalists, and it seems to be making mistakes in all of them. (I was not invited to speak with it, and frankly, I cannot imagine why Particle6 didn’t want to schedule that meeting.)

In one particularly odd interview with Piers Morgan and actor Tom Conti, which was recorded and posted online, Norwood seems to malfunction and abruptly begin speaking Chinese.

When discussing the movie that Norwood is promoting, Conti asks if the other actors are also AI-generated. Norwood responds by saying that human writers, editors, and directors were involved.

“You didn’t really understand the question,” Conti replies. “Are the other actors on the screen with you real actors, or are they computer-generated images? Do you know?”

“Ah, right. You’re asking about the other actors in Misaligned,” Norwood starts. “They’re all digital twins just like me. It’s a hybrid production which m—”

Norwood stops talking for a second, then starts speaking in Chinese for over 10 seconds.

“Tilly, if I could just ask you a question,” Morgan says, looking puzzled. “It’s Piers again … You seem to be speaking Chinese completely randomly for no reason. Why did you do that?” he asks.

“Oh, my apologies,” the AI replies. “It seems I had a little hiccup there. I certainly didn’t mean to start speaking Chinese or impersonate Piers. Sometimes my wires get a bit crossed, you know?”

When AI bots try to act like humans, they can be so convincing that people forget they’re chatting with a computer, which can lead to dangerous outcomes. But Norwood is so surprisingly bad at talking to people that it’s almost suspicious.

Perhaps Particle6 Group calculated that people would be more likely to talk about Norwood if they were making fun of it, figuring no one would take its upcoming film seriously.
