title: iOS 27.2’s First Developer Beta Brings These Features to Some iPhones
snippet: The developer beta includes updates to apps like Facetime and Podcasts.
fullText:
Just two days after Apple released iOS 27 to the general public, the tech giant released the first developer beta for iOS 27.2. While iOS 27 brought Siri AI and more to your device, this early look at iOS 27.2 shows Siri AI expanding to other languages and a few upgrades in other apps, like Facetime.

If you’re wondering what happened to iOS 27.1, Apple has said the foldable iPhone Duo will launch on 27.1 next month, and all devices will be able to update to 27.2 sometime later.

Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it only on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.2, so the update might be buggy and battery life may be short — it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, more features could end up landing on your iPhone when Apple releases iOS 27.2. 

Here are some features developers can try now in the first iOS 27.2 developer beta.

Siri AI in more languages

In iOS 27, Siri AI is only available in English. But the first developer beta of iOS 27.2 expands Siri AI to French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish.

Apple previously said Siri AI would expand to these additional languages, so this shows the company moving quickly on that promise.

Use front and rear cameras simultaneously in Facetime

In the first developer beta of iOS 27.2, you can use your front and rear facing cameras at the same time in Facetime calls. This allows you to Facetime call with a larger group of people — you don’t have to squeeze everyone into a single frame in order to see the person on the other end of the call. However, everyone on the call needs to be on iOS 27 or later for this feature to work.

	

			

Refreshed Podcasts options

The Podcasts app also gets an update in the first iOS 27.2 developer beta. The beta introduces two rows to the top of the Home tab within the app: New Episodes and Continue Playing. This can help you keep track of what podcasts are new and what podcasts you still have to finish. 

It’s a small, pleasant addition to the interface, and I appreciate how it helps keep my podcasts organized.

Apple TV profile expansion

In the first developer beta of iOS 27.2, you can create TV Profiles in your Apple TV app. You can assign a profile to your child or someone else and ensure your preferences aren’t messed with. 

So if you’re tired of being recommended kids shows after letting your child watch the series Shape Island, you can create a profile for your child and let them watch those quirky little shapes all they want. (But also, it’s possible that I like Shape Island more than my son does, so you should check it out.)

Apple TV multiview on iOS

Another Apple TV update in the iOS 27.2 developer beta is Multiview. Developers who subscribe to Apple TV can watch up to four live sports streams, including streams from Major League Soccer and Formula 1, at once. That way, you don’t miss an important game, or you can look at a map of the racecourse while watching feeds from driver-view cameras.

Updated Health app

Developers can see a redesigned Health app in the first developer beta of iOS 27.2. However, the redesign is expected to launch sometime later this year, despite being featured in this beta.

Those are a few of the new features developers can try now with the first developer beta of iOS 27.2. There will likely be more betas before the OS is released to the public. Apple has not said when exactly it will release iOS 27.2 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices in October.

For more, here’s what to know about iOS 27 and why your battery might be draining faster after updating. You can also check out why the iPhone Duo will launch with iOS 27.1.

title: The Clicks Communicator Ships in December With More RAM and New Mobile Service
snippet: A new video shows off the BlackBerry-like phone’s features, including the speech-to-text Prompt Key, Message Hub and new Clicks Mobile wireless service.
fullText:
At a time when nearly every phone-maker is raising prices and cutting memory, one company is bucking the trend by adding more RAM.

The $649 Blackberry-inspired Clicks Communicator phone will launch in December, but the company behind it just announced that the unreleased handset will have a larger battery and more RAM than originally expected. Clicks Technology, better known for its keyboard cases and Power Keyboard accessory, released a video on Friday sharing a number of upgrades, feature details and news about the launch.

The Clicks Communicator will ship with 12GB of RAM (up from the promised 8GB) and a 4,350-mAh battery (up from 4,000 mAh). Given this year’s trends, it is absolutely wild that the company is adding more RAM while keeping the previously announced preorder price of $499. Google, Motorola, Samsung and, most recently, Apple, have raised prices on most of their phones, including the new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max, citing higher RAM and component costs driven by the increased demand for memory by AI data centers.

Clicks Technology announced the keyboard phone at CES in January. The marquee feature is a built-in physical keyboard that is similar to the one found on the company’s keyboard cases. The design was inspired in part by using a Motorola Razr’s cover screen inside a Clicks keyboard case for the phone. After receiving an unexpectedly high number of preorders, Clicks was able to upgrade the design and features, including the processor. 

I took this photo in March. On the left is a dummy prototype of the Clicks Communicator, and next to it is a Motorola Razr (closed) inside a Clicks Keyboard case. Notice the Razr has the Niagara launcher on its cover screen.Patrick Holland/CNET

Turns out, plenty of people want a thoughtfully designed handset that combines old-school features — including a keyboard, dedicated notification light and headphone jack — with a modern smartphone focused on messaging, calls and efficiency. The Communicator, designed by a former BlackBerry designer, is the phone I’ve been looking forward to most this year.

People who preordered the Clicks Communicator can now configure their phone’s color, keyboard layout, charging covers and accessories on the company’s website. If you’re considering buying one, you can preorder it for $499 ($150 off) until Sept. 30.

The Communicator is sold unlocked, meaning that you can use your current carrier’s nano SIM card or eSIM with it. But you also have the option to use the company’s new voice and data service for phone called Clicks Mobile. It’ll run on AT&T in the US and Vodafone in the UK.

The video also showcases a number of Communicator features in depth. Here are a handful that stood out.

The Communicator will ship with the game Brick Breaker.Patrick Holland/CNET

Clicks Care

You can extend the warranty beyond a year and add accidental damage protection. “If something happens, even from day one, we’ll ship you a replacement,” says Jeff Gadway, Clicks Technology co-founder, in the video. Clicks Care will be available in the US and Canada for $129 for two years.

Prompt Key 

While the physical keyboard is the main attraction, you can press the Prompt Key for speech-to-text input. The feature is powered by an on-device model, but Clicks Technology is exploring ways for Communicator owners to use other apps and services for voice input. The Prompt Key can also be used to bring up Gemini when you’re not in a text field.

Signal Light

An LED loop around the Prompt Key glows in different colors for calendar reminders, tasks and to indicate incoming calls and messages. You can customize the Signal Light with different colors for different contacts and priorities. The light will flash in different patterns to distinguish between a call and a message. This is what Pixel HiLight on the Pixel 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max should have been; instead, that sits mostly dormant on the back of the phone and only glows during calls or when Gemini is “listening” to a prompt. 

Quick replies

You can read and respond to message previews straight from the home screen, without opening the app. Gadway explains that the company is working to make it possible to reply and dismiss message previews using just keyboard shortcuts: No need to touch the screen.

Message Hub is a quick way to reply to messages without having to open apps.Patrick Holland/CNET

Message Hub

A curated pop-up on the home screen, the hub prioritizes incoming message notifications according to your Signal Light preferences. You can hop into the Message Hub at any time by pressing the Prompt Key or the Clicks Key on the keyboard.

Customizable hardware keyboard

The physical keyboard has a red Clicks Key that can be used to trigger shortcuts, similar to Click’s keyboard cases and the Power Keyboard. You can also reassign the bottom-row keys to take screenshots, switch between apps and perform other tasks.

Locking your phone

You can lock the Click Communicator by double-tapping the app list on the home screen. The phone uses a special version of Niagara Launcher, which displays apps in a list that you can navigate by sliding your finger along the right side of the screen.

The Saffiano leather charging covers will cost $79.Patrick Holland/CNET

MagSafe charging covers

The phone supports 15W Qi2 wireless charging and has a swappable backplate available in a variety of colors. There will be two Saffiano leather charging covers.

Case, bumper and screen protector

Accessory maker Dbrand is creating a $39 case for the new phone called MNML (pronounced “minimal”) and a $35 screen protector. Clicks is selling its own bumper case for $49 — it gives off a strong iPhone 4 bumper vibe.

The Clicks Communicator’s specs

Smoke, clover and onyx colors

4.03″ AMOLED display with Gorilla Glass, 120Hz

MediaTek Dimensity 8300 (MT8883), 4nm processor

12GB RAM

256GB storage, expandable via microSD up to 2TB

4,350-mAh lithium-ion battery, rated for more than 800 charge cycles

USB-C port

15W Qi2 wireless charging

50-megapixel main camera with OIS

24-megapixel selfie camera

Android 17 with software updates through Android 20 and 5 years of security updates

Wi-Fi 6

Bluetooth 5.4

NFC with Google Pay

3.5mm headphone jack

Three microphones

Dual speakers

title: SwiftKey ‘AI voice’ is Pixel 11’s Rambler voice-to-text for other Android phones, works offline
snippet: Rambler in Gboard is perhaps one of the best Pixel 11 features, delivering powerful voice-to-text backed up by AI models. Once you’ve used it, it’s hard to switch back to anything else, but the Microsoft-owned SwiftKey is testing out a new “AI voice” feature that brings the core functionality of Pixel 11’s Rambler to basically any other Android phone. more…
fullText:
Rambler in Gboard is perhaps one of the best Pixel 11 features, delivering powerful voice-to-text backed up by AI models. Once you’ve used it, it’s hard to switch back to anything else, but the Microsoft-owned SwiftKey is testing out a new “AI voice” feature that brings the core functionality of Pixel 11’s Rambler to basically any other Android phone.

Available in the latest SwiftKey for Android beta release (v9.13.16.4), “AI voice” is an enhanced voice-to-text feature that allows you to speak and then let the AI step in to clean up filler words, format text, and more. In other words, it’s Pixel 11 Rambler, just without the exclusivity.

You tap a microphone icon to get started, with no live preview showing (the one thing we don’t love about Rambler) and a checkmark button ending the session, leaving the AI to process the result. 

Android Central notes that you’ll need to download an offline language model for “AI voice” to work, which is one big difference – it works offline, no servers required. The publication says that testing the feature on a Fold 8 required only 163MB of storage and worked with the device fully offline, something you can’t do with Rambler on the Pixel 11 series. Droid-Life also tested it out, finding that you can’t use voice commands to edit the test as Rambler allows, but it gets the job done.

	

While it initially seemed like Rambler might not be a Pixel exclusive, that’s where we’re at right now, so “AI voice” in SwiftKey is probably a good alternative for many. Wispr Flow is also available, as we previously covered, though its lack of keyboard integration can be a bit annoying at times.

You can download the SwiftKey for Android beta through the Play Store.

title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
snippet: Truecaller says the one-way sharing requirement would hand a commercially valuable proprietary asset to telecom operators.
fullText:
India has extended its anti-spam regime to require caller-ID and call-management apps to share users’ spam reports with telecom operators, prompting spam-blocking app maker Truecaller to call the ruling anti-competitive.

On Friday, the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), the country’s telecom regulator, amended rules governing commercial communications, making it mandatory for caller-ID and call-management apps that let users flag calls as spam or junk to send those reports to a blockchain-based platform maintained by telecom operators. The platform tracks commercial communications and enforces anti-spam rules.

The change, TRAI said, is intended to broaden the pool of spam reports available for action against spammers, effectively connecting reports collected by apps with the telecom industry’s enforcement infrastructure.

However, Truecaller told TechCrunch that it sees this requirement as a “one-way exchange” that is “anti-competitive,” arguing that it transfers commercially valuable data from call-management apps like itself to telecom operators.

India is Truecaller’s largest market, accounting for well over 350 million of its more than 500 million monthly active users globally. The Stockholm-based company uses community reports alongside automated detection and other signals to identify and block spam calls.

The rules come as India grapples with spam and fraudulent calls at enormous scale. In its report in February, Truecaller said its users in the country encountered around 42 billion spam calls in 2025, including calls that were blocked, labeled, or ignored. The company also stated that it blocked nearly 12 billion spam calls during the year.

It is not the first time Truecaller and the Indian regulator have been at odds over how spam calls should be handled. The Swedish company previously objected to restrictions preventing call-management apps from automatically labeling calls from certain government-designated number ranges as spam. It argued that the exemption could allow unwanted calls to escape its filters.

However, Friday’s amendments retain that restriction and have barred call-management apps from blanket blocking, filtering, or spam-tagging calls from designated number series used for promotional, service, and transactional communications. Individual users can still choose to block such calls on their own devices, the regulator said.

“While our data and user sentiment clearly show that spam has skyrocketed due to this free pass to spammers, we have been compliant with this since late last year,” a Truecaller spokesperson said.

Sumeysh Srivastava, a partner at New Delhi-based consulting firm The Quantum Hub, who leads its telecom-regulation policy work, said the latest change bridges two distinct layers: Telecom operators provide the underlying network and run the blockchain-based anti-spam system, while caller-ID apps operate on top of the network to identify and filter calls.

That raises technical and jurisdictional questions, Srivastava told TechCrunch, including what reporting standards apps will have to follow and how the requirement will be enforced against companies that are not themselves telecom operators.

A March draft proposed (PDF) using India’s IT laws to enforce the requirement. However, Srivastava pointed out that the new announcement did not say whether that enforcement mechanism was retained in the final rules.

It is also unclear how much information the apps will actually have to provide under the updated regulation. Kazim Rizvi, founding director of New Delhi-based policy think tank The Dialogue, told TechCrunch that requiring an app to transmit a specific spam report made by a user is materially different from requiring it to share the broader datasets, reputation signals, or analytical systems it uses to identify suspicious calls.

The rules will need clarity on what information must be transmitted, how users are notified or asked for consent, and how that data can subsequently be retained and used, Rizvi said.

TRAI did not respond to TechCrunch’s questions about what information apps would be required to share and whether the rule would also apply to spam-reporting features built into smartphone operating systems and dialers such as Android and iOS.

New rules for AI-powered calls

The amendments also address the growing use of software and AI voice agents to make calls. Calls made automatically, without a person directly dialing the number, will now fall under TRAI’s application-to-person (A2P) framework. That includes robocalls and calls using prerecorded or artificial voices.

Companies using such systems will have to declare their use and the phone numbers involved to their telecom operators in advance. Undeclared A2P calls will be treated as spam, TRAI said.

The key test, Srivastava said, is how a call is initiated, rather than simply whether it uses an AI-generated voice, leaving some uncertainty around AI-assisted calls that involve human initiation.

Satya N. Gupta, a former additional secretary at TRAI, told TechCrunch that the new rules do not restrict businesses from using AI or other automated calling technologies, but instead require them to disclose their use to telecom operators.

Telecom operators will also be allowed to levy a termination charge of up to 5 paise (about 0.052 cents) per minute on A2P calls. However, calls made using certain designated number ranges will be exempt.

Rizvi told TechCrunch that the new definition could also cover calls made using software even when a person is still involved, such as calls from contact centers and click-to-call services. “Without that distinction, the A2P category risks becoming broader than the regulatory harm it is intended to address,” he said.

title: iOS 27: My favorite new iPhone features (other than AI)
snippet: Apple released iOS 27 to everyone this week, and the headlining changes are Siri AI and the array of new Apple Intelligence features. However, the update also includes plenty of non-AI features. Here are a few of my favorite iOS 27 features (other than Siri and AI). more…
fullText:
Apple released iOS 27 to everyone this week, and the headlining changes are Siri AI and the array of new Apple Intelligence features. However, the update also includes plenty of non-AI features.

Here are a few of my favorite iOS 27 features (other than Siri and AI).

The new Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features are fantastic in iOS 27, but there are some others: 

In the Music app, Apple has updated AutoMix with new transitions. I was a big fan of the initial version of AutoMix that launched in iOS 26, and the new transitions in iOS 27 are noticeably better and more immersive.

In the Photos app, iCloud Shared Albums now offer full-resolution sharing. This is a big upgrade that makes it significantly easier to share photos and videos with others without compromising image quality.

You can now set an independent volume for alarms in the Clock app. This new option is in the Settings app under “Sounds & Haptics.” This means your alarms and timers no longer have to match your ringtone volume.

iOS 27 adds an all-new extra-large widget size for your Home Screen. There are full-screen widgets for apps like Music, Photos, Weather, and Calendar.

You can now swipe away the Now Playing widget from the Lock Screen in iOS 27. 

On the Lock Screen, you can now move the clock to the top widget row, so it no longer gets in the way of your wallpaper.

In the Photos app, you can now save a specific video frame as a photo. This means you no longer have to manually take a screenshot of a video you’ve already taken to get a specific frame as a separate photo.

The Apple Pay checkout flow has been significantly overhauled, making it a lot easier to switch between payment cards.

iOS 27 adds landscape support to more apps, which is great as someone who keeps their iPhone docked at their desk all day. This includes apps like Music, Reminders, Weather, and more.

The Find My app has a new design in iOS 27, plus more flexible sharing options. In particular, I like that the new design shows me more specific location information without having to tap on a specific person.

When you copy something to your iPhone’s clipboard in iOS 27, you’ll see a built-in paste shortcut above the keyboard the next text field you go to. This makes it a lot quicker to copy and paste text, links, photos, and more between apps.

In CarPlay, there’s now an audio scrubber that lets you skip to different parts of a song or podcast right on your car’s display.

What are your favorite non-AI features in iOS 27? Let us know down in the comments.

title: I Used AI to Animate Old Family Photos. One Was Creepy, but the Other Was Heartwarming
snippet: Can memories be memorialized forever with AI? Or is there something uncanny about feeding childhood pictures to the machine?
fullText:
I miss the time when things were more tangible. Photo albums, CDs, cameras and books. Nowadays, everything is centralized on one device or stored in the cloud, sometimes accidentally erased, not always owned by you and forever out of sight. But it’s this very technology that can also bring these memories and milestones back into focus, with a little help from AI.

The hug your younger self photo was a fun example, but I wanted to take it further and animate some old photos to turn them into a gift. It can make a good gift if you’ve got a big family birthday or a wedding anniversary coming up, and it can also be a beautiful way to keep a loved one who has passed close, if the AI is accurate enough in regenerating your moments. It could also be a special exercise to connect family members who have never met, like grandparents and their grandkids.

I came across AliveMoment, a moving-memory tool, which is essentially image-to-video technology. I chose this product for its no-prompt process, as well as its photo restoration features, because that grainy old photo look won’t fly here. AliveMoment was released in August 2025 and runs on a credit-based subscription model (more on that later).

Time for a walk down memory lane.

Getting set up

The biggest issue I had was hunting down my old photos, as many are in boxes and hard drives back in Australia, where I grew up. Most of my photos live on my Facebook profile or in the cloud, so I needed to spend some time going through what I had. 

I wanted to find a photo of my grandparents, who I think about often. I always felt as though they were my parents, as they were big travelers and migrated from England to Australia. I’ve traveled to more than 50 countries and moved to America, while my parents never even had a passport. 

So, my first task was to do some digging. I found a couple of cute baby photos with my siblings, as well as one with my nanna, but the quality of all three was bad. 

I uploaded one of them to AliveMoment to see what options I had to improve it. I could choose between a few animation types, including adding a wave or a hug. Given this first photo was of my siblings and me, I selected “playful motion.”

AliveMoment/Screenshot by CNET

To proceed, I was prompted to sign up, and it processed the photo for a few seconds before my “live moment” was ready. But before I could view it, I had to purchase a subscription. Check the fine print because although it’s presented as per-credit pricing, you’re charged the first week, month or two months upfront. I chose the cheapest plan ($2.47 per “moment” credit) just to test it out. 

Make sure you delete it before it renews, as that weekly plan is $60 per month, and this isn’t the kind of AI tool you need a recurring subscription for. I’ve noticed a lot of AI tools have sneaky pricing structures like this, most likely to capture as many one-time customers as possible.

Creepy or heart-warming?

Next, I got into the dashboard and could see the full range of features. I could restore, retake or relive a photo. I reuploaded the photo of my siblings to turn it into a motion photo. I had to use an extra credit for it to be in color.

Here was the original photo: 

Amanda Smith/CNET

And this was the short video AI animated:

Amanda Smith/AliveMoment

Creepy. It doesn’t look like us.

Next, I wanted to see if it could do better with adults. I uploaded a photo of my nanna and me, and picked the “warm hug” animation. 

This was the original still:

Amanda Smith/CNET

And this was the video: 

Amanda Smith/AliveMoment

And oh my gosh, this pulled at my heart when I watched it. It captured our connection and even got my dimple. I’ll be saving this video on my phone. Worth $9.90. 

At this point, I ran out of coins. If you were going to use Alivemoment for a bigger animation project, not just bringing to life single photos, you’d need to buy the top plan, but it doesn’t come cheap. 

The verdict on using AI to animate old photos

I don’t think it’s worth doing for baby photos, as AI can only predict future features, especially when using old, low-quality photos. Use it for adult stills, as it’s much more accurate. 

I can see many different fun use cases for animated memories. I’ll keep repeating this exercise as the technology improves over time. I’m especially interested in watching what AI can do for the bereaved.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Amanda Smith

title: iPhone Duo could be very hard to get at launch, per report
snippet: iPhone Duo pre-orders open next month, and a new analyst report indicates the device could be in even shorter supply at launch than expected. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo pre-orders open next month, and a new analyst report indicates the device could be in even shorter supply at launch than expected. Here are the details.

‘Hinge constraints’ will reportedly limit iPhone Duo supply at launch

Following months of rumors about Apple’s first foldable iPhone, last week Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo.

Unlike the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, iPhone Duo won’t ship in the typical September timeframe. Instead, pre-orders will open Friday, October 16 ahead of the first deliveries October 23.

We’ve seen reports before saying that supply could be very constrained. And the latest update from analyst Jeff Pu adds further corroboration to that claim.

In a research note seen by 9to5Mac, Pu writes that iPhone Duo units shipped in 2026 are now expected to be only 6 million, down from his previous 7 million estimate.

The reason isn’t a lack of demand, but rather “hinge constraints” that are causing production slowdowns.

For context, Pu estimates 72 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models will ship by the end of the year—about 12x the iPhone Duo estimate.

So if you’re hoping to get an iPhone Duo at launch, it might be quite the challenge despite having the highest-ever $1,999 starting price for an iPhone.

title: Y Combinator insurance tech alum Angle Health hits $2.7B valuation
snippet: Angle Health has grown to 5,000 customers and become profitable by helping small businesses get "level-funded" health insurance.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

1:24 PM PDT · September 18, 2026

Image Credits:TravelCouples / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

These days, it’s rare to hear of a startup founded in 2019, or one not focused on AI agents, raising a hefty Series C. But health insurance startup Angle Health announced Friday that it raised a $200 million Series C, alongside a $400 million tender offer, at a $2.7 billion valuation. The round was led by Vitruvian Partners with participation from Town Hall Ventures, Blumberg Capital, Portage Ventures, PruVen Capital, and Y Combinator. The tender offer allows employees to cash out some of their shares, the company told TechCrunch. It expects the round to close later this month.

Angle Health, a winter 2020 YC alum, helps small businesses obtain and manage what’s known as “level-funded health plans.” These are plans that land between fully insured and self-funded plans. In fully insured plans, the carrier takes all the risks; such plans are more expensive but costs are predictable. With self-funded plans, the company covers the expenses and costs can be unpredictable. With level-funded plans, businesses make predictable payments to carriers, are insured against higher-than-expected costs, and can potentially save money by getting a share of the surplus back if expenses stay low.

Angle says these plans can make health insurance more affordable for small businesses. It’s an AI-powered platform that helps small businesses choose and manage plans, integrating with payroll and HR systems. The startup says it serves over 5,000 businesses and is profitable.

title: iOS 27 adds scam-prevention feature to iPhone, here’s how to enable it
snippet: iOS 27 introduces a new security feature called ‘Impersonation Risk Detection’ that helps protect you against scams, but it’s off by default. Here’s what the feature does, and how to enable it. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 introduces a new security feature called ‘Impersonation Risk Detection’ that helps protect you against scams, but it’s off by default. Here’s what the feature does, and how to enable it.

Impersonation Risk Detection in iOS 27 can detect suspicious activity in real time to prevent scams

Every day around the world, people get tricked into sharing sensitive information like bank details or other financial info with bad actors.

This commonly happens via text messages, emails, or phone calls to iPhone or Android devices. And while iOS has built-in tools like call and message screening, those tools can’t prevent a scam if you choose to take action on it.

But iOS 27 introduces a new level of scam-prevention with a security feature called ‘Impersonation Risk Detection.’

Here’s what it does, per Apple’s website:

Impersonation Risk Detection helps protect against active social engineering scams. In these scams, an attacker might pose as a bank, government agency, or someone you trust to pressure or guide you into making a payment or changing your account details. Traditional security measures like two-factor authentication can’t always detect this kind of scam. That’s because you’re taking the action, even though you’ve been tricked or pressured.

Impersonation Risk Detection analyzes information about your device and Apple Account to help detect signs of an active scam. Based on this analysis, it returns a risk level to the app. The app receives only the risk level, not the underlying information used to generate it. The app decides what to do next. For example, it might ask you to verify your identity, add a delay, or show a warning.

You can turn Impersonation Risk Detection on in iOS 27 by going to Settings ⇾ Privacy & Security ⇾ Impersonation Risk Detection then toggling on ‘Share with App Developers.’

Impersonation Risk Detection is only available in supported apps, and Apple hasn’t published a list of those apps at the moment. But once enabled, it provides the app with a “risk level” while omitting the underlying information driving it. Risk levels include:

Unknown: No evidence of suspicious activity was detected

Medium: Some signs of suspicious activity were detected

High: Significant signs of suspicious activity were detected

Once the app has this risk level, it decides what action to take. For example, it may prompt you to offer additional authentication, or show a warning message related to scams.

For more details on how the feature works using ‘Trust Insights,’ see our coverage here.

title: Apple pushes UK court to lift secrecy around encryption backdoor order
snippet: In a hearing today, Apple challenged the UK government’s refusal to publicly confirm whether it has issued an order requiring the company to provide access to encrypted user data. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
In a hearing today, Apple challenged the UK government’s refusal to publicly confirm whether it has issued an order requiring the company to provide access to encrypted user data. Here are the details.

A bit of context

Early last year, The Washington Post reported that the British government had secretly ordered Apple to create a security backdoor into all iCloud content uploaded by users worldwide.

The order itself was also subject to strict secrecy rules, preventing even Apple from publicly confirming or discussing the demand.

The British government has maintained a policy of neither confirming nor denying the existence of individual orders of this kind, while companies subject to them are also restricted from disclosing that they have received one.

As a result of the reported but officially unconfirmed order, Apple removed the option to enable Advanced Data Protection (ADP) for iCloud users in the UK.

That’s because with ADP enabled, iCloud Backup and other additional categories of iCloud data are end-to-end encrypted. So instead of complying with the UK’s backdoor order, Apple stopped offering ADP to new users in the UK altogether, even though the original order reportedly applied to users worldwide.

At this point, Apple’s fight with the UK government was two-pronged: it was challenging both the underlying demand for access to encrypted data and the secrecy rules preventing it from publicly discussing that demand.

In April, 2025, judges rejected the UK government’s attempt to keep even the basic details of Apple’s legal challenge secret, ruling that disclosing the existence of the case would not harm national security.

A few months after that, the British government gave up on requiring data from American users as part of the secret mandate, as a result of pressure from the White House. The demand did not disappear entirely, however: Britain later issued a new notice targeting Apple users in the UK.

Fast-forward to a few weeks ago, when it emerged that Apple had launched a second legal challenge against the UK government after the original worldwide order was replaced by a new one specifically targeting British users.

Which brings us to today.

Apple challenges mandate secrecy

As reported by Reuters, Apple today challenged the UK government’s continued refusal to confirm or deny the existence of the new Technical Capability Notice during a hearing before the Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) in London.

According to Reuters, Apple’s lawyer argued that the government’s secrecy policy prevents meaningful public discussion of the case, and undermines the principle of open justice.

From the report:

At Thursday’s hearing at the IPT, Ben ​Jaffey, the lawyer for campaign groups, Privacy International and Liberty, said the government’s position had “become farcical”.

“The horse has long bolted,” he noted, ‌meaning ⁠it was already public knowledge.

U.S. politicians and officials had publicly referred to the original notice while unnamed UK government sources had also confirmed it to the press, he said.

Both he and Apple’s lawyer said that the UK government’s NCND policy was an affront to open justice and prevented meaningful public discussion of the issue.

To be clear, today’s hearing focused on the secrecy surrounding the order, not on whether the UK government was legally entitled to demand access to Apple’s encrypted data in the first place.

Following today’s hearing, the IPT will now decide whether the government can continue relying on its “neither confirm nor deny” policy in this case. Reuters says a full hearing on Apple’s challenge to the underlying Technical Capability Notice is unlikely before next year.

Boox just announced three new e-ink devices on Android 16; the largest tablet is available now, but you’ll have to wait a little longer for the updated Palma 3.

E-ink devices have taken off in the last couple of years for a couple of reasons. The main reasoning that comes to mind is the natural disconnect that comes from using an e-ink device instead of a traditional modern OLED smartphone or tablet. Another likely has something to do with the universal appeal of an e-reader or note-taking device that lets you access apps from the Google Play Store.

Boox announced three new additions to its lineup of Android e-ink devices:

Boox Note Air6 C

Boox Note Mini C

Boox Palma 3

All three will run Android 16 out of the box, which is notable because the latest public version of Android is only one generation ahead of that. It wouldn’t have been a surprise if these devices were still a generation or two behind that. Two could be considered tablets, while the Palma is a generational upgrade to the company’s beloved compact e-reader that looks like an Android phone, at first glance.

	

The Note Air6 C is the only model Boox says is available starting today. It’s the workhorse of the three, with a new internal processor and a reasonable 3,700mAh battery. The new processor boosts the Note Air6 C’s performance with features like Dual Notes that let you annotate two documents in split-screen mode.

Boox mentions the large Android tablet also has new AI features for transcripts and document scanning. But the real improvement might just be an upgraded refresh rate that increases performance by up to 40%. Refresh rates have always been a sore point for e-ink tablets, but it’s always come with the territory for a paper-like display.

The 10.3-inch tablet has a color display that works with the included Pen3 stylus. It also wouldn’t be a Boox tablet without a front-light with temperature controls for any-time viewing.

The Note Mini C isn’t available to order just yet. It’s an 8.52-inch Android e-ink tablet aimed at users who need a little more portability from Boox devices. Similar to the Note Air6 C, it has a Kaleido 3 color e-ink display with a front light, as well as an octa-core processor. It has a little less battery power at 3,150mAh. On an e-ink tablet, that still goes a long way.

We’re also getting an upgraded model in the Palma series with the Palma 3. The form factor has grown more popular since Boox began teasing the Picco. The Palma 3 is slightly bigger and has a 6.13-inch display.

This version has a “refined anodized aluminum frame” instead of the plastic exterior seen on the previous models. The rear panel is made from fiberglass that has a “paper-textured” feel. Under that panel sits a 3,950mAh battery, which hasn’t changed from even the original Palma.

Boox hasn’t announced a release date for the Note Mini C or the Palma 3, but the Note Air6 C is available now. The Note Air6 C starts at $579. Boox’s Note Mini C is priced at $579, too, and the Palma 3 will be $339 at launch.

title: Samsung’s battery upgrades for Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro leak – is it enough?
snippet: A new leak reveals the battery sizes of Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro including some long overdue upgrades, but do you think it’s enough? more…
fullText:
A new leak reveals the battery sizes of Samsung’s upcoming Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro including some long overdue upgrades, but do you think it’s enough?

Following Samsung’s adoption of silicon-carbon battery tech on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series, it was inevitable that the Galaxy S27 series would jump on board. That’s not directly confirmed yet, but a regulatory leak (via GSMArena) offers a look at the rated capacities of Samsung’s new flagships.

These are rated capacities, with advertised capacity generally being a bit higher. As a comparison, the Galaxy S26 Ultra has an advertised battery capacity of 4,855 mAh, but an advertised capacity of 5,000 mAh. So, with that in mind:

Galaxy S27 Ultra: Rated 5,534 mAh | Advertised likely 5,700~ mAh 

Galaxy S27 Pro: Rated 5,087 mAh | Advertised likely 5,200~ mAh 

There’s no direct comparison for the Pro model, but the Galaxy S26 sits at 4,300 mAh at around the same physical size, so this is a huge jump. 

	

For Samsung’s full-size flagship, the Galaxy S27 Ultra is looking at a jump of around 700 mAh. It’s only 14%, but that’s a considerable step up after years of stagnation. Both devices are also listed with 60W wired charging.

But, in a world where silicon-carbon batteries are pushing Android flagships upwards of 6,000, 7,000, and even bigger batteries. The Oppo Find X10, for example, is rumored to pack in an 8,000 mAh battery when it debuts later this month. 

What do you think? Did Samsung do enough? Sound off in the comments below.

title: HomeKit Weekly: Homey’s new Device Updates feature shows what Matter was supposed to be all along
snippet: Firmware updates have been the weakest link for a decade with smart homes. Every sensor, light bulb, and smart lock in your house runs software that should be updated regularly. This is on top of even if they have software updates. Homey just announced a fix for a big piece of that, and the way it handles Matter devices is the part that Apple Home users should take note of. more…
fullText:
Firmware updates have been the weakest link for a decade with smart homes. Every sensor, light bulb, and smart lock in your house runs software that should be updated regularly. This is on top of even if they have software updates. Homey just announced a fix for a big piece of that, and the way it handles Matter devices is the part that Apple Home users should take note of.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

Device updates from one place

Homey’s new Device Updates feature lets you update Matter, Z-Wave, and Zigbee devices directly from the Homey Mobile App or Web App. You can update a Matter light, install a security patch for a Z-Wave lock, or improve a Zigbee sensor’s reliability, all without ever opening a manufacturer’s app. You start the update, and Homey handles the rest, including delivery, progress tracking, and a notification when it’s done. Updates are available in More > Settings > Device Updates or in each device’s Maintenance settings.

For Z-Wave and Zigbee gear, updates are delivered via their respective Homey apps, so availability depends on the developer and manufacturer. The launch list of supported vendors is already pretty solid: IKEA, Aeotec, INNR, Niko, Inovelli, Zooz, frient, ThirdReality, EcoDim, HeatIt, Namron, amina, CTM Lyng, and Nous have added support, with more to come soon.

“Device firmware rarely gets updated because the process is cumbersome,” said Stefan Witkamp, CEO at Athom. “By handling device updates inside Homey, we make it practical for both users and developers. That makes the whole smart home more dependable.”

The Matter part is the real story

For Matter devices, Homey doesn’t rely on manufacturer apps at all, and manufacturers don’t need to update their Homey app for it to work. Homey checks the Connectivity Standards Alliance’s Distributed Compliance Ledger for available Matter firmware updates. The DCL provides the firmware version, download URL, file size, checksum, and applicability information. Homey then retrieves the firmware from the manufacturer-provided URL and delivers it to the device using Matter’s standardized OTA update mechanism.

The DCL is basically a trusted public registry for Matter products, run by the same organization that certifies them and is behind the Matter standard itself. Manufacturers publish firmware update metadata to the Matter Distributed Compliance Ledger, allowing Homey to discover and grab the available updates.

This means that the update path for Matter devices isn’t tied to any one company’s app or cloud service. It’s part of the actual Matter standard itself, verified by the certification body, and any Matter controller could implement it.

If you don’t see an update you expect, it’s usually because the device’s Homey app doesn’t offer it yet, or the manufacturer hasn’t published one. Device Updates is available on Homey Cloud, Homey Pro (2023 through 2026), Homey Pro mini, and Homey Self-Hosted Server, and requires v13.2.0 or later of the Homey Mobile App.

Eve devices now work with Homey, thanks to Matter

Speaking of Matter doing what it promised, there’s a second piece of Homey news worth covering. With Homey Pro and Homey Pro mini acting as Matter Controllers and Thread Border Routers, Matter-enabled Eve devices now work with Homey. That covers favorites I’ve written about plenty in this column: Eve Energy, Eve Door & Window, Eve Motion, Eve Thermo, Eve Weather, Eve MotionBlinds, and more.

Eve has always been one of the most trusted and privacy-focused brands in the smart home (with deep Apple Home integration), with no cloud service, no registration, and no tracking. If you’re running Eve gear in Apple Home today, nothing changes. What’s changed is that the same Thread and Matter foundation that made Eve great in Apple Home now makes it portable across other platforms, and that flexibility is exactly the point of the Matter standard. It’s a protocol vs a platform.

Wrap up

For years, the smart home industry has promised interoperability and delivered walled gardens with extra steps. Simply working with the big 3-4 major platforms isn’t enough. This Homey news is what the long-term benefits of Matter are proving to bring: firmware updates going through the standard body itself.

Matter has taken plenty of criticism for moving slowly, but features like this are why it matters.

title: Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking powers Gemini Live, Gmail, & Keep
snippet: Google today announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking as its “most advanced live dialogue models yet.” more…
fullText:
Google today announced Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking as its “most advanced live dialogue models yet.”

Following the launch of 3.1 Flash Live in March, the new models aim to “make conversing with AI feel more intuitive and intelligent.” 

As the name suggests, Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking offers “increased intelligence and multi-step reasoning.” It’s meant for high-complexity tasks like the recently launched Gmail Live (conversational search), Docs Live (draft generation and editing), and Keep Live (note creation). The model is also beginning to roll out to Gemini Live today.

3.8 Live Extended Thinking “reasons and speaks simultaneously.”

	

It delivers increased intelligence for complex workflows while maintaining an uninterrupted conversational flow — using early verbal cues like “Let me check that…” to acknowledge prompts naturally, and live progress narration to walk users through multi-step background tasks as they progress.

In terms of benchmarks: 

“…the #1 overall spot on Artificial Analysis’ Speech to Speech Quality Index (82.6)”

“…leads in agentic task completion with 68.6% on τ-Voice”

“…35.1% on Sierra’s τ-Voice-banking benchmark”

“…strong reasoning capabilities, scoring 97.7% on Big Bench Audio, while maintaining a highly competitive price point compared to other frontier models.”

Meanwhile, the Gemini 3.8 Live base model offers “conversational intelligence with fluid dialogue and visual grounding.” The model can process “visual inputs in near real-time,” with tools and API calls executing in the background while the conversation continues. 

Users can expect the model to “acknowledge requests and keep chatting while tasks finish in the background.” Additionally, it can detect and transition between 97 supported languages mid-conversation. 

It’s “built for scale and cost efficiency” with a “second place in the Speech Agent Arena.” Gemini 3.8 Live will power AI Mode’s Search Live experience.

title: iPhone 18 Pro vs. Pixel 11 Pro: The New Apple and Google Pro Phones Are Quite Different
snippet: Both Apple and Google raised the price of their 2026 flagship phones by $100, but which one deserves the higher price tag? I compared the specs of iPhone 18 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro to find out.
fullText:
The iPhone Duo might have stolen the spotlight at Apple’s Surprise and Shine event last week, but the latest high-end iPhone 18 Pro remains the go-to option for creatives. With the inclusion of variable aperture that can control light exposure for photography and long battery life, Apple’s new Pro phone is well equipped for media capture. But the new model is more expensive than ever. At its $1,199 starting price, the phone is $100 more than the base iPhone 17 Pro and Google’s new $1,099 Pixel 11 Pro.

While Google’s Pixel 11 Pro received its own $100 price hike over last year’s 10 Pro — likely influenced by the ongoing memory shortage that’s making electronics more expensive — the phone also received camera upgrades like a larger sensor on its 48-megapixel telephoto camera that promises a 30% increase in light capture (versus the 10 Pro). That telephoto camera supports the 11 Pro’s 30x digital zoom as well as its 120x Pro Zoom — the latter using generative AI to clean up photos taken at that distance.

Both phones have a big focus on photography, but after that, Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro and Google’s Pixel 11 Pro differ dramatically. They have designs that will suit different crowds and functions, and spotlight the best of iOS 27 and Android 17, respectively. I’ve taken a closer look at each phone’s biggest features, so you can figure out whether the iPhone 18 Pro or the Pixel 11 Pro is the better fit for you.

The Google Pixel 11 Pro brought some fun colors.Andrew Lanxon/CNET

While the iPhone 18 Pro and the Pixel 11 Pro have similar designs to the phones they’ve replaced — the iPhone 17 Pro and the Pixel 10 Pro, respectively — each phone has an entirely different style.

The iPhone 18 Pro sports an aluminum unibody design and, this year, a cleaner monotone look rather than the dual-tone finish of the 17 Pro. The 18 Pro comes in four colors: burgundy red, glacier blue, silver and black. 

The back of the Pixel 11 Pro highlights its full-width camera bar with an added edge-to-edge glass for a more uniform look. It comes in canyon (an orange-pinkish shade), fog white, olive green and obsidian black. Both the Pixel and the iPhone have color-matching frames, giving them a seamless look. In the hand, the Pixel 11 Pro will feel lighter than the iPhone 18 Pro, with the phones weighing in at 204 grams and 211 grams, respectively — in both cases roughly the same as a medium apple.

Both phones have a 6.3-inch OLED display with support for a dynamic 120Hz refresh rate, and are IP68-rated for water and dust resistance — making them safe to take to environments like the beach where sand and water won’t get inside.

The Dynamic Island is smaller on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max (right) than last year’s 17 Pro Max (left).Patrick Holland/CNET

On the iPhone, there’s a new, smaller Dynamic Island that serves as the cutout for the selfie camera and Apple’s Face ID sensor. That space can now show up to three Live Activities at once, letting you glance at active timers or the status of a rideshare vehicle that’s en route to pick you up. The display is protected with Ceramic Shield 2, which is the same as the 17 Pro, and it has held up quite well after a year of use, so I expect similar durability here.

The Pixel 11 Pro has a traditional selfie camera cutout on the front, but its display should shine brighter in sunny environments with its 3,600-nit peak brightness. The iPhone 18 Pro, by comparison, has an also-bright 3,000-nit peak brightness. Google’s display sports Corning’s Gorilla Glass Victus 2 protection, and includes an ultrasonic fingerprint sensor underneath the screen. The Pixel 11 Pro also supports facial identification that is assisted by its front-facing camera and machine learning.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11 Pro cameras

The iPhone 18 Pro supports variable aperture on its main camera.Patrick Holland/CNET

Apple and Google have worked on camera advancements in both hardware and software on their latest phones.

The iPhone 18 Pro has a variable aperture on its 48-megapixel main camera. It can manually adjust the aperture between four options (ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, and ƒ/4.0 f-stops) to control the amount of light hitting the sensor. It is accompanied by a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera and a 48-megapixel telephoto sensor with support for 4x optical zoom and 8x hybrid zoom.

CNET’s Patrick Holland confirmed in his review that the aperture automatically adjusts itself when shooting between 1x and 3.9x magnification. It is great for shutterbugs and can shoot some amazing shots in the dark. 

In comparison, the Google Pixel 11 Pro has a 50-megapixel main camera, a bigger 48-megapixel telephoto sensor with 5x optical zoom, and a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera. It’s got a new Camera Looks feature for built-in color profiles. CNET’s Andrew Lanxon tested and enjoyed using it: “I don’t think Google takes full advantage of this tool yet, but it’s a step in the right direction and a welcome addition for casual shutterbugs who love to simply snap away without worrying about editing later.”

For selfies, you get an 18-megapixel front camera on the new iPhone and a 42-megapixel front camera on the Google phone. Apple’s smarts include automatic framing based on the number of people in the selfie — letting you switch between horizontal and vertical without rotating your phone — and Pro controls to quickly adjust settings like aperture and shutter speed, among other things. On the other hand, the Pixel has a new Magic Capture mode (on the rear cameras), which records a short video clip and then uses AI to select the best still frames from it — and you can manually pick your favorite stills as well. 

Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11 Pro: processor and battery

The Pixel 11 Pro’s display is impressive, but its gaming performance isn’t exceptional.David Lumb/CNET

Apple’s new iPhone runs on the in-house A20 Pro chip, which is based on the 2nm process. That means the processor is denser and may have helped make room for the 18 Pro to get a larger vapor chamber to help keep the phone running cool under intensive use. In his review, Patrick said that “gaming on the iPhone 18 Pro Max has been a blast.”

He notes that the iPhone 18 Pro got warm only when downloading apps and game files (some as large as 28GB) or when charging — but not to the extent that it would be a concern. This is one of the best improvements since my iPhone 17 Pro Max used to get warm in regular use, depending on the ambient temperature.

For comparison, the Pixel 11 Pro has the new Tensor G6 processor, which powers new software and camera tricks. In my usage, it has been smooth in daily life. However, it gets warm to the touch in 10 minutes or more of gaming. While the Pixel 11 Pro’s screen makes games look good, CNET Managing Editor David Lumb finds the phone underpowered for gaming, noticing it struggles with higher graphics settings. The iPhone remains a better choice if you’re a mobile gamer, and Apple’s App Store includes several console-quality games for the iPhone that, when purchased, also work for Mac and Apple TV.

Another Apple upgrade comes in the form of battery life. The iPhone 18 Pro is claimed to last longer and charge faster than its predecessor. In CNET’s review, Patrick pointed out that the battery life “matches that of the 17 Pro and Pro Max.” It can last an entire day, but when you push it to the limits and drain the battery, it can charge faster than before.

In our 30-minute wired charging test, the 18 Pro went from empty to 82% charge. In the same test, the Pixel 11 Pro went from 55% to 88% with its 30-watt charging speed. If you opt for the Pro XL model, you get faster 45-watt charging, which can deliver more charge in the same amount of time.

Apple iPhone 18 Pro vs. Google Pixel 11 Pro: Extra features

The iPhone 18 Pro runs iOS 27, which squashes bugs and comes with a new set of features. It has improved voice-to-text capabilities and a smoother user interface. The new Apple iPhone also offers Focus Tracking and Reference Image features in the Camera app. The former can help you track a subject more efficiently, while Reference Image is like a digital version of a film negative. It grabs the pixel data at the time the image was taken before it goes through Apple’s image pipeline, so you can check the authenticity of the photo. That can be especially helpful since many Apple Intelligence features let you alter photos substantially, such as how Spatial Reframing lets you adjust the angle of a subject using generative AI.

On the other hand, the Pixel 11 Pro has many new Gemini Intelligence features, such as voice-to-text capabilities (Rambler) that filter out filler words when sending a message, or the ability to communicate in ASL via the Pixel camera. I’ve also enjoyed the new Camera Looks, while HiLight (a notification light on the camera bar that’s initially just for phone calls and Gemini) has been disappointing. title: Apple Music in iOS 27: Five new features just added for iPhone
snippet: iOS 27 brings new features to apps like Apple Wallet, Calendar, Notes, Maps, and more. Apple Music adds a variety of improvements too, including five new features outlined below. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 brings new features to apps like Apple Wallet, Calendar, Notes, Maps, and more. Apple Music adds a variety of improvements too, including five new features outlined below.

#1: Landscape mode

iOS 27 adds support for landscape layouts to many system apps, including Apple Music. The feature will be especially nice on iPhone Duo, but other iPhone models benefit too.

With landscape mode, you can view music artwork alongside playback controls just like in portrait orientation. 

More important to me though, lyrics are now available side-by-side with artwork. I’ve found this a great way to enjoy music while my iPhone is docked on a desk or kitchen charger.

#2: AutoMix improvements

AutoMix debuted last year in iOS 26, but Apple has upgraded and expanded it this year in iOS 27.

Per Apple’s press release:

AutoMix has added a whole new layer of energy and excitement to the experience with even better transitions that feel more immersive and engaging for listeners. AutoMix will also be available on Apple Music in tvOS and on HomePod.

Like my colleague Chance, I’ve definitely found AutoMix transitions improved this year. In iOS 26 I sometimes loved the feature and other times found it frustrating. In iOS 27 so far it’s been almost entirely a positive for me.

#3: New design for artist pages

Artist pages get a refreshed look in iOS 27, with a design that takes inspiration from iOS 26.4’s updates for albums and playlists.

Like albums, artist pages now have fullscreen color backgrounds that complement their header image. You can see several examples above.

Artist pages also make key controls more convenient to access, and their featured music title is more prominently displayed than before.

#4: Friends playlist

Apple’s roster of weekly-updated ‘Made for You’ playlists expands in iOS 27 with a new Friends playlist. Per Apple’s description:

The best of what your friends are listening to. Updated every Thursday.

The playlist is a convenient new way to get a taste of your friends’ current favorites. Each track shows you which friend is listening to it too.

iOS 27 introduces an extra-large widget size for the first time, and Apple Music takes advantage of it more than any other app.

Apple Music has three new extra-large widgets: 

Recently Played

Recommendations

Top Charts

These widgets can be added to your Home Screen or Today view, offering more flexibility in personalizing your iPhone.

Which new Apple Music features in iOS 27 are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments.

Apple Music is available for $11.99/month, or you can get it as part of the Apple One bundle.

title: Clicks Communicator lands in December with 12GB RAM, two months of free data
snippet: Clicks — the company bringing physical keyboards back to mobile — is getting ready to ship its first-ever Android smartphone, and it’s shaping up to be a pretty interesting device. Ahead of its launch later this year, the company is upgrading a handful of the Clicks Communicator’s specs and announcing new accessories, protection coverage options, and eSIM plans. more…
fullText:
Clicks — the company bringing physical keyboards back to mobile — is getting ready to ship its first-ever Android smartphone, and it’s shaping up to be a pretty interesting device. Ahead of its launch later this year, the company is upgrading a handful of the Clicks Communicator’s specs and announcing new accessories, protection coverage options, and eSIM plans.

When the company announced the Clicks Communicator back at CES this year, it was primarily pitched as a secondary device meant to pair with your main smartphone. It seems like the team has heard from its potential customers that some might be satisfied with this being their main smartphone, which has prompted a handful of changes to improve the overall experience.

By far, the biggest upgrade is a move from 8GB to 12GB of RAM, something I’ll be calling a “reverse Pixel 11 Pro” situation. While other smartphone makers are doing whatever they can to reduce RAM — while increasing prices along the way — Clicks is adding additional memory to the device to better futureproof the phone. Its upgrade policy isn’t quite on par with Google or Samsung, but three promised OS upgrades and five years of security updates will, at the very least, pull your Communicator through to around 2032. Clicks has also moved its launch platform to Android 17 out of the box and bumped its battery capacity up to 4,350mAh. 

On the accessory side, Clicks and Dbrand are bringing the latter’s new MNML cases to the device, along with its Prism screen protector that includes a self-aligning tray — is there any other way? Clicks will also continue to offer its bumper Ring case for those looking for a more minimal approach to protection. Dbrand’s case and screen protector will run you $39 and $35, respectively, while the Ring bumper case is $49. Additional Charging Covers, allowing you to switch up your phone’s design, will also be available for $50 or $80, depending on material.

	

Finally, Clicks is launching both a protection plan and eSIM options for its users. Clicks Care is a $129 protection plan that delivers replacements or repairs for accidental damage over a two-year term with a $49 deductible; it’ll be available in the US and Canada. Clicks Mobile, meanwhile, is a new MVNO offering that brings voice and data to the Communicator via eSIM in the US and UK. Subscribers will receive two months of free service when activating their device at launch.

Clicks Communicator is set to ship in December, with reservation holders getting invites today to configure their final orders. September 30th — about two weeks away — is the last day to pre-order the device at its $499 launch price; starting October 1st, it moves to its base MSRP of $650. Anyone who scores the device as its cheaper starting price won’t be asked to pay more for its battery or RAM upgrades.

title: iPadOS 27.2 adds convenient new feature from the Mac
snippet: iPadOS 27.2 arrived in beta this week, and beyond adding the redesigned Health app, Apple has also brought over a recent Mac feature: a Siri popup when text is selected. more…
fullText:
iPadOS 27.2 arrived in beta this week, and beyond adding the redesigned Health app, Apple has also brought over a recent Mac feature: a Siri popup when text is selected.

Siri AI is the tentpole addition to iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and companion releases. And as such, Apple offers lots of ways to access the new, supercharged assistant.

On iPad you can invoke Siri via a “Siri” or “Hey Siri” voice prompt, pull down from the top of the screen, use the new Siri option in the edit menu, open the new Siri app, or my personal favorite: use CMD + Space to open Spotlight and ask Siri a question from there.

But iPadOS 27.2 adds yet another option that’s borrowed directly from the Mac.

In macOS 27 Golden Gate, in many situations when you select some text, a small Siri icon appears in the top-left corner of the selection. When you hover over the icon with your cursor, it expands to offer an ‘Ask Siri’ text box.

This wasn’t available in iPadOS 27. But now, if you have a trackpad connected to your iPad, that same behavior is available in iPadOS 27.2.

As seen in the images above, the new Siri icon starts out small and stays out of the way, but it’s very convenient to just hover over it to make the ‘Ask Siri’ box appear.

If you don’t have a trackpad attached, selecting text will still reveal the full edit menu where you can tap to open Siri. But it’s a more smooth and seamless experience with a trackpad.

macOS is full of small productivity-focused features like this that speed up everyday interactions, yet are missing from iPadOS. So it’s exciting to see such a recent Mac feature be brought over to the iPad.

title: Apple releases Xcode 27.1 beta, enabling iPhone Duo app development
snippet: Apple has released Xcode 27.1 beta 1 for developers. This version specifically enables app development that targets the new foldable iPhone Duo. more…
fullText:
Apple has released Xcode 27.1 beta 1 for developers. This version specifically enables app development that targets the new foldable iPhone Duo.

While iPhone Duo doesn’t launch until October, today’s Xcode release gives developers a chance to prepare for initial iPhone Duo support. 

Properly optimizing most apps for iPhone Duo will probably take more than a few weeks for most apps. However, Xcode 27.1 meets Apple’s promise to release dev tools before the end of September.

Apps built against Apple’s iOS 26 SDK will need to be updated for iOS 27 for basic iPhone Duo support.

Apps made for iOS 27.1 and later will take full advantage of the larger display. Still, there are a lot of sizing and layout considerations that developers need to consider when shipping proper app support.

While the device isn’t out yet, Xcode 27.1 beta also gives developers the chance to virtually experience their apps on the iPhone Duo simulator.

Xcode 27.1 beta is available to download from Apple’s developer webpage here.

The release follows the introduction of Xcode 27.2 beta earlier this week. Apple is shipping iOS 27.2 as the next software update for iPhones running iOS 27.0 with the exception of the iPhone Duo.

 It will run iOS 27.1, a version designed for the foldable device, before syncing up with the rest of the iPhone lineup in a later version.

iPhone Duo will be available for pre-order on October 16 and ships October 23. Pricing starts at $1999.

title: Samsung Phone Users Can Now Sync Photos and Video to Google
snippet: Syncing to Microsoft OneDrive will end on Sept. 30.
fullText:
One cloud in, one cloud out. Samsung phone users can now sync photos and videos in their Gallery app to Google, as native Microsoft OneDrive integration ends Sept. 30. The update will roll out over the coming days, and availability may vary depending on account type, device model or region.

Tech insider Ice Universe viewed the new feature and posted images on X, noting that you may now see a new “Sync photos and videos” option in Gallery Settings.

As detailed on this Google page, you must have a compatible Samsung device running Android 13 or newer and a personal Google account. To find out which Android version you have, go to Settings > About phone > Software information, then look for the Android version. If you need to create a Google account, the details are here.

After syncing Gallery to Google Photos, users can view and share multimedia from their Samsung devices, the Google Photos app and photos.google.com. But there are limitations. Google Workspace accounts can’t use it, and synced items can’t be viewed in Google features such as memories and highlights, live albums or search unless you back up photos and videos via Google Photos.

Also, Google Accounts supervised by parents are ineligible to use the feature.

Google says that you can back up photos, videos, albums, device folders such as downloads or screenshots, and metadata such as timestamps, location, and favorites status.

Representatives for Samsung and Google did not immediately respond to requests for further comment.

Syncing Samsung Gallery to Google Photos is optional, but storing photos and videos only in the Gallery will quickly eat up phone storage space. Open the Samsung Gallery app on your phone, then tap the three-line hamburger menu at the bottom right. Select Settings, then Sync Photos and videos. Choose a Google account from the instructions and grant permission to sync media.

Deleting items from either Samsung Gallery or Google Photos will remove them from both apps and from your cloud storage. Editing photos in either app will also show up everywhere.

Users can also turn off syncing at any time, and previously backed up items remain safely stored in their Google Account.

title: Google confirms Pixel phones were exploited in ‘targeted’ attack related to modem
snippet: Google has confirmed that a “limited” number of Pixel phones were attacked by a vulnerability related to the modem on the device. more…
fullText:
Google has confirmed that a “limited” number of Pixel phones were attacked by a vulnerability related to the modem on the device.

As part of the September 2026 security update, Google patched over 200 security vulnerabilities, but specifically calls out that one of those was actively exploited in the wild.

Note: There are indications that CVE-2026-58704 may be under limited, targeted exploitation.

The issue is related to the modem, with a bypass that requires no user interaction. CVE-2026-58704 is described as follows:

In Cellular Modem, there is a possible permission bypass due to a logic error in the code. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

Exact details of how the vulnerability was exploited are unclear – as well as which models were affected – but CISA (via The Hacker News) says that it was exploited on Pixel phones, explaining that “Google Pixel devices contain an improper authorization vulnerability in the cellular modem.” Combined with Google’s announcement, this was used in the wild, apparently to hack “targeted” devices. CISA issued a notice that this is a “known exploited vulnerability,” explaining that “this type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise.” TechCrunch notes that this is called a “zero-click” attack, adding that Google hadn’t replied to a request for comment around the vulnerability being exploited and who was exploiting it.

	

If you’re on a Pixel phone, updating to the September 2026 patch, rolling out now, fixes the issue.

title: PDF Expert update adds handwriting recognition, expands Apple Pencil support, more
snippet: Readdle updated PDF Expert for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 this week, adding several new features, including searchable handwriting in 29 languages. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Readdle updated PDF Expert for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 this week, adding several new features, including searchable handwriting in 29 languages. Here are the details.

PDF Expert now indexes handwritten notes

Readdle’s classic PDF editor, PDF Expert, was updated this week with several features that leverage new possibilities introduced with iOS 27 and iPadOS 27.

Chief among them is a new Handwriting Recognition feature, which works both within individual PDFs and across the user’s entire library, including existing handwritten annotations and notes added in other apps.

PDF Expert now indexes these notes as regular text, making it easier to find something the user might remember jotting down but can’t quite recall where it was.

The company notes that Handwriting Recognition currently works with 29 languages, matching the language support offered by Apple’s new PKStrokeRecognizer API. Presumably, as Apple expands language support for the API, PDF Expert and its users will benefit as well.

Importantly, Handwriting Recognition and library-wide search are available to PDF Expert Premium users. Free users can still use the Text tool to write by hand and have their handwriting converted to typed text as they write.

Additionally, the update adds support for the Apple Pencil Pro’s squeeze gesture, which opens PDF Expert’s tool palette.

Here’s Readdle:

title: Another Intel iMac has joined Apple’s vintage products list
snippet: After adding three MacBook models to its obsolete products list last month, Apple today updated its vintage products list to include the 2019 21.5-inch iMac with Retina 4K display. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
After adding three MacBook models to its obsolete products list last month, Apple today updated its vintage products list to include the 2019 21.5-inch iMac with Retina 4K display. Here are the details.

iMac (Retina 4K, 21.5-inch, 2019) now vintage worldwide

Apple maintains a list of vintage and obsolete products, which lets users know whether older devices are still eligible for hardware service and replacement parts.

The company considers a product vintage once it has been off the market for more than five but less than seven years. Products may become obsolete once Apple has stopped distributing them for more than seven years.

Apple doesn’t necessarily move products to the obsolete list as soon as they cross that threshold, as service and parts availability can vary by product. That said, once a product is classified as obsolete, Apple and its authorized service providers generally stop offering hardware service for it, and parts can no longer be ordered.

Today, the company added the iMac (Retina 4K, 21.5-inch, 2019) to its vintage products list, which means it may still be eligible for hardware service and replacement parts, but they’re subject to availability.

In practice, if you own this iMac and have been putting off a repair, it might be a good idea to get it serviced sooner rather than later.

title: Samsung Gallery is adding Google Photos backup to replace OneDrive
snippet: New updates are starting to roll out that will let Samsung Gallery replace its OneDrive integration with Google Photos support. more…
fullText:
New updates are starting to roll out that will let Samsung Gallery replace its OneDrive integration with Google Photos support.

Earlier this year, Samsung Gallery removed integration with OneDrive and, in turn, also removed native cloud backup for Galaxy users. Users could, of course, use apps from Microsoft, Google, Amazon, or any other number of providers, but there was nothing built into Samsung’s own Gallery app anymore.

Now, Samsung is confirming its replacement.

In an update to the “Gallery Cloud Sync” app on Samsung devices, the company says:

	

Gallery Cloud Sync is a service that safely backs up your precious memories to Google Cloud, allowing you to enjoy them seamlessly on all your devices at any time. View photos taken on your smartphone right away on your tablet.

Easy and secure backup: Safely store your Gallery photos, videos, and albums in the Cloud.

Seamless multi-device sync: No matter which device you use, your Gallery is always kept identical and up to date.

Google Cloud-based reliability: Provides a fast and stable environment through Google’s trusted cloud storage.

Edited for formatting

The mention of “Google Cloud” here is a bit misleading, as Samsung Gallery is adopting direct Google Photos integration, as shown by an early preview of this functionality by @WigettaGaming and SammyGuru writer “That Josh Guy” on Twitter/X. It’s not live just yet – at least in our testing – but Samsung Gallery will offer support for “Sync with Google,” including the ability to see available storage via the Gallery app, choosing which albums to sync, and what data conditions must be met to sync.

Samsung requires the “Gallery Cloud Sync” app and “Samsung Cloud” to both be updated, but it seems a Gallery app update or perhaps even a full system update will be required to get this working fully.

Google Photos integration like this has existed for a few years now, previously being added to the OnePlus Gallery app in 2024 and on devices from Xiaomi and select other brands. Google’s support page on the topic does not yet mention Samsung.

Samsung Gallery will still let existing OneDrive users sync their photos through September 30, but it’s great to see a replacement lined up.

title: Android Canary 2609 adds ‘Require unlock for Quick Settings’ on Pixel
snippet: Google today is rolling out Android Canary 2609 with another update to Quick Settings that lets you require an unlock before making changes. more…
fullText:
Google today is rolling out Android Canary 2609 with another update to Quick Settings that lets you require an unlock before making changes.

ZP11.260821.010 with the September 2026 security patch is available for the Pixel 10a, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Pixel 9a, Pixel 9, Pixel 9 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro XL, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 8a, Pixel 8, Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 7a, Pixel 7 Pro, Pixel 7, Pixel 6a, Pixel Fold, and Pixel Tablet.

Google notes that “support for Pixel 11 devices will be added with the next Canary release. Additionally, Google has dropped support for the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro.

As always, “Canary builds are highly experimental and are NOT recommended for general use.”

	

Require unlock for Quick Settings

Go to Settings > Display & touch > Lock screen for the new “Require unlock for Quick Settings” toggle that is off by default: “To prevent unauthorized changes, you must unlock your device to use Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Mobile Data, and Airplane Mode.”

When enabled, you can still open the Quick Settings panel from the lockscreen, but tapping on those key Tiles will prompt you to fingerprint or PIN unlock. The flashlight, rotation, dark theme, etc. don’t require authorization.

Audio streams Quick Settings Tile

Additionally, the “Voice broadcast” Tile moves from system apps to Connectivity.

Notification Intelligence 

Appearing on older devices (Pixel 8) with just the existing Notification cooldown feature.
